Mammograms are widely used to help detect breast cancer, but they may also offer insight into heart health.

The routine X-ray screening may identify breast arterial calcification (BAC), which is the presence of calcium deposits within the walls of the small arteries in the breast.

On a mammogram, BAC is commonly identified as thin, white, parallel lines that give a “tram-track” appearance.

While BAC is harmless to the breasts, it is associated with a significantly higher risk of cardiovascular disease. A 2022 study found women with BAC were 51% more likely to develop heart disease or experience a stroke than those without it.

Laxmi Mehta, MD, a cardiologist at The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, mentioned BAC is associated with cardiovascular risk factors, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol. Additionally, BAC has been connected to:.

“The reasons for BAC resulting in higher risks for cardiovascular disease are not definitely determined; however, there are some potential mechanisms, one being that they share similar risk factors that result in vascular injury or metabolic stress that result in vascular calcification and atherosclerosis,” Mehta told Healthline.

Cheng-Han Chen, MD, interventional cardiologist and medical director of the Structural Heart Program at MemorialCare Saddleback Medical Center, added that because BAC and heart disease share many of the same risk factors, “calcium in breast arteries therefore suggests disease in the heart (coronary) and brain arteries as well,” he told Healthline.

While 1 in 39 females in the United States dies from breast cancer each year, cardiovascular disease causes one out of every three deaths, resulting in 1 death per minute.

“Cardiovascular disease is still the most common cause of death in premenopausal women,” Richard Reitherman, MD, PhD, a radiologist and medical director of breast imaging at MemorialCare Breast Center at Orange Coast Medical Center, told Healthline.

“The presentation of cardiovascular disease in premenopausal women is notoriously different than in postmenopausal women, primarily [because] there are no typical symptoms such as chest pain.”.

Reitherman stated that a prevalent and common health screening procedure such as a mammogram can lead to the early identification of women with silent cardiovascular disease.

“Cardiovascular outcome studies that have included breast arterial calcifications as a risk factor are increasingly reported in the medical literature,” he said.

“The hope is that identifying younger women with silent cardiovascular risks [like BAC along with] appropriate integrated risk identification, analysis, and interventions can significantly reduce mortality in this age group.”.

Mehta noted there are several reasons BAC has been overlooked as a risk factor for heart disease.

“Mammograms are completed for assessment of breast cancer, and BAC has been historically an ‘incidental’ finding, which is not clinically relevant from an oncologic standpoint,” she said.

Additionally, there is no standardization on quantification of BAC severity, nor is it a required component of mammogram reports, noted Mehta.

However, routine reporting of BAC on mammograms is an urgent goal of the American College of Radiology, Society of Breast Imaging, and Medicare, remarked Reitherman.

In fact, it is gaining traction in the United States. A fresh Maryland law, passed on October 1, requires mammography centers to notify women when a BAC is detected on their mammogram.

“Automated identification and reporting of these calcifications detected on screening mammograms will become increasingly prevalent in the coming months [and] years,” mentioned Reitherman.

The next step is to identify this group of women to primary care physicians so that appropriate risk evaluation can take place, Reitherman added.

In addition to doctors routinely screening for conditions related to heart disease, such as diabetes, high blood pressure, and high cholesterol, he hopes BAC will also be routinely considered.

“Under current development are protocols to identify patients needing a cardiologist’s training and expertise to appropriately stratify this group of patients,” said Reitherman.

“The common healthcare behavior [of] having regular mammograms not only reduces risk of morbidity and mortality from breast cancer but will hopefully contribute to the reduction of morbidity and mortality from cardiovascular disease in younger women.”.

He stated this type of integrated healthcare approach demonstrates cross-specialty integration and coordination among women, radiologists, and their healthcare providers to improve women’s lives.

“This is an amazing game-changing opportunity,” Reitherman stated.

Mehta said it’s reasonable for women to ask if BAC is present on their mammogram report.

“But if it is not uniformly reported by the radiologist, the individual clinician may not have the answer,” she noted.

More research is needed before BAC on mammograms can be used routinely to predict heart disease.

Finding out your BAC could provide additional information to help you and your doctors decide how aggressively to address your cardiovascular risk factors, Chen said.

Industry observers note that reitherman agreed. “The goal of reducing morbidity and mortality from any cause such as cardiovascular disease is based on recognition of risk factors, followed by appropriate lifestyle and pharmacologic interventions,” he mentioned.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • If you're tired of feeling like you're never quite enough, or that you're never going to get "there" (wherever there is), consider the following questions.
  • Sources indicate that instead of skimming through these questions the way you might read a typical blog post, I'd like to suggest that you wait until you have a quiet moment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

If you're tired of feeling like you're never quite enough, or that you're never going to get "there" (wherever there is), consider the following questions.

Sources indicate that instead of skimming through these questions the way you might read a typical blog post, I'd like to suggest that you wait until you have a quiet moment. Sit or lie down. Read the words silently or out loud, and really consider them. Try them on, the way you might try on a piece of clothing to see how they fit.

Notice what happens inside your body as you read. See if any of these ideas can sink in. If they can't right now, that's OK, too.

Sometimes old programming runs deep and can feel hard to change. With patience and practice, old beliefs can be questioned and updated, and upcoming ways of thinking and being can take root.

So get comfortable, take a slow, deep breath, and consider these possibilities.

What if I remembered that self-critical thoughts aren't necessarily facts, and I didn't have to believe everything I think?

What if I could begin choosing fresh thoughts and beliefs that are kinder, more supportive, and actually feel good?

What if I got off my own back, got on my own side, and decided that I am a good person doing the best I can?

What if I remembered that kindness, compassion, and encouragement help people grow, while berating, pressure, and perfectionism often get in the way?

What if my worth didn't depend on how much I accomplished, how productive I was, or how well I did things?

What if I allowed myself to do things imperfectly, and let good enough be good enough?

What if I could let myself be a beginner, make mistakes, change my mind, and learn as I go, rather than expecting myself to get everything right every time?

What if I spent less time living in worst-case scenarios about the future and more time in the present moment?

What if I slowed down, ever so slightly, and sprinkled small moments of conscious breathing and quiet awareness throughout my day?

What if I stepped out of the never-ending race to get somewhere and spent more moments in actual, factual reality?

What if I softened my gaze when I looked at myself and softened my thoughts when I thought about myself?

What if I spent less time comparing myself to others, remembering that I know nothing about what their lives actually feel like on the inside, and instead offered myself more moments of grace?

What if I became curious about what enoughness feels like?

What if I decided that, in this exact moment, I am already enough? I can still do what I'm moved to do, pursue what matters to me, and take care of what needs to be done without staying trapped on the endless treadmill of never-enoughness.

What if I simply stated, Thank you for what I have, kept the welcome mat out, and stayed open to whatever comes next?

What if, just for today, I let myself be enough?

Nearly 3 million pages of military records from the War of 1812 are finally online

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812.
  • While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the fresh documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after 16 years of painstaking work, the National Archives and its collaborators have finally completed digitizing over 90,000 pension applications submitted to the United States government following the War of 1812. The project is more than just preservation for preservation’s sake. The roughly 2.8 million pages contain long-forgotten and missing details about 19th century Americans, their families, and their everyday lives.

While archivists previously digitized a similar collection related to the American Revolutionary War, the fresh documents will help fill in knowledge gaps between early 19th century military events and the 1850 federal census. Patricia Oxley, president of the Federation of Genealogical Societies (FGS), explained the project was also incredibly time-sensitive.

“In the specific case of the War of 1812 pension records, there is an added priority due to their frail state where not acting may mean sacrificing these for future generations,” Oxley stated in a recent announcement.

It has been revealed that the somewhat fresh United States of America declared war on the United Kingdom on June 18, 1812, citing objections to trade restrictions with France amid the Napoleonic Wars, as well as the Royal Navy’s impressment of American sailors. Although the conflict famously included a British attack on Washington D.C. that resulted in the burning of the White House and U.S. Capitol, little shifted geopolitically between the two nations following the ratification of the Treaty of Ghent on February 17, 1815. The U.S. tallied around 15,000 casualties, while the U.K. and Canada saw about 10,700 deaths. Another 9,000 Indigenous fighters died while enlisted between the two sides.

Today’s military records are meticulously documented and stored digitally, but applying for benefits such as pensions was a much more labor-intensive process during the 19th century. With the burden of proof on each applicant, veterans were required to supply lengthy accounts of their service. Each War of 1812 pension file is liable to contain not just combat information, but the names and personal details of fellow soldiers, family members, spouses, and countless other relations.

“Our people have been asking for the War of 1812 pension records for some time, and I expect this collection to be very popular based on the rich war time detail it contains,” added Brian Hansen, general manager at Fold3, Ancestry’s military records service and National Archives collaborator.

Industry observers note that the collection also includes a full-text search feature using handwriting recognition technology. This lets consumers explore the files based on every named individual, and not simply the primary veteran applicants. The pension records are at the moment available for free on Fold3’s website, and are being added to the National Archives catalog on a rolling basis.

Correction 11/20/26 9:30 a.m. EST: A previous version of this article incorrectly stated the pension archive contained around 7 million files. This was based on an initial assessment from researchers in 2010. The article has been updated to reflect the more accurate tally.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alpitronic, the tech giant behind IONNA’s fast chargers, is investing nearly $34 million in a newly introduced South Carolina factory. It’ll build 400 kW DC fast chargers, plus a 1 megawatt (MW) system that can charge cars and heavy-duty trucks.

In a recent development, the $33.94 million project in Fort Mill is expected to create 70 jobs, the South Carolina Department of Commerce unveiled Wednesday. It’ll be the Bolzano, Italy-based Alpitronic’s first operation in South Carolina, just across the state line from its North American headquarters in Charlotte.

According to recent reports, the HYC400 packs up to 400 kW into a single unit. If you’ve stopped at an IONNA Rechargery, you may have already plugged into one.

The HYC1000 works differently. A separate power cabinet can send up to 1 MW across as many as eight vehicles at once, shifting power between them as their charging needs change. Operators can configure it with CCS or NACS plugs for passenger EVs or a Megawatt Charging System (MCS) plug for compatible heavy-duty trucks.

Alpitronic’s 400 kW chargers were already being made in Wisconsin for Mercedes-Benz High-Power Charging in 2024. Alpitronic Americas CEO Patrik Herrnegger remarked the Fort Mill plant “will put US production under our direct control, bring us closer to our customers, and enable us to serve them more efficiently.”.

Sources indicate that the 173,315-square-foot site at 3560 Stateview Blvd. (pictured above) will also house a testing lab, repair operations, a warehouse, logistics space, and offices. South Carolina approved job development credits and awarded York County a $200,000 grant to help pay for building improvements.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve been paying any attention to the shooter market these past few months, you won’t be surprised to learn that Battlefield 6 has been an unprecedented success for EA, and the Battlefield series as a whole.

In a recent development, the game managed to sell over 7 million units at launch, climbing to the top of the charts anywhere you look, including setting fresh series concurrent player records on Steam. Thanks to new data, we now better understand the true scale of this launch.

According to recent reports, the latest Circana report, which looks at game and hardware sales in the United States, has arrived. This iteration covers the month of October, which is when Battlefield 6 was released.

Battlefield 6 was the top-selling game across all platforms during October - which isn’t surprising. It has overtaken NBA 2K26 to become 2025’s best-selling game year-to-date, making it the best-selling Battlefield game ever.

In October alone, the game sold more than the lifetime sales of Battlefield 1, previously the best-selling entry in the franchise.

Battlefield 6 even set records beyond just its own series, having now produced the highest single-month dollar sales (physical and digital) total for any full game released in the last three years. The previous record holder was 2022’s Modern Warfare 2.

It has been revealed that november’s report, which is set to arrive midway through December, will show, once and for all, whether Battlefield 6 has been able to overtake Black Ops 7. With one exception, Call of Duty games have, for more than a decade, topped the best-selling year-to-date chart. Regardless of the quality of the individual titles, or the competition in any given year, nothing has been able to shake that dominance.

It has been revealed that given all this momentum, Battlefield 6 has a shot at dethroning Call of Duty this year, beating Black Ops 7 to become the year’s best-seller. You never want to count out the sheer popularity of Call of Duty among casual players, however, which is what’s going to make December’s report all the more interesting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most mid-cycle refreshes touch only the surface stuff: a new grille, new headlights, new wheel designs. They typically don’t venture too far into the mechanicals. Toyota flipped the script in its approach to the 2027 Sienna hybrid minivan, mostly leaving the visuals alone and focusing instead on the substantive bits. The result is a minivan that’s more upgraded than it looks.

In a recent development, much like a person who is very bad at seeing those magic-eye illusions, you could stare at a picture of the 2027 Sienna all day and nothing fresh would make itself apparent. The exterior is unchanged, although one paint color (Cypress) has been dropped in favor of a new hue (Storm Cloud). The trims have also been rejiggered: The Limited is gone, and the XSE picks up some of its features and becomes the new penultimate trim beneath Platinum. Otherwise, every inch of mid-cycle-refresh effort went into the underlying tech and the powertrain.

See all results for used cars for sale near 49505.

Recent findings suggest that the base LE loses its 8.0-inch infotainment screen as Toyota democratizes digital real estate, granting every Sienna a 12.3-inch infotainment screen and a 12.3-inch gauge display. New LED cabin lighting arrives, and the rear-seat entertainment picks up major upgrades with native apps and a new touchscreen. The sound-deadening material behind the dashboard has also been tweaked.

It has been revealed that we saved the best bits for last. The 2027 Sienna adopts Toyota’s latest (sixth-gen) hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the Lexus ES. The old nickel-metal hydride battery is replaced by a lithium-ion pack that stores more energy, and it feeds a redesigned and more efficient electric motor to produce a combined 251 horsepower—six more than its predecessor. All-wheel-drive models energize the rear axle with an additional motor, though that doesn’t raise output any. Toyota estimates a 7.5-second run to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive guise, rising to 7.6 with all-wheel drive (since there’s more mass and no extra oomph). Either way, that’s 0.3 to 0.4 second quicker than the 2026 Sienna. Our long-term 2021 Toyota Sienna Limited AWD did the deed in 7.6 seconds.

Industry observers note that the 2026 Sienna earned EPA fuel-economy estimates of 36 city, 36 highway, and 36 combined for front-wheel-drive models and 35/36/35 for all-wheel-drive variants. While official numbers have not yet been released for the 2027 model, Toyota claims city improvements of 3 mpg (FWD) and 4 mpg (AWD), with combined estimates rising between 1 and 2 mpg.

In a recent development, because these changes might not seem like much on paper, Toyota gave us access to both a 2026 Sienna and a 2027 Sienna to better experience the changes. And we’re glad we had that opportunity, because the revised Sienna does make for a vastly improved driving experience.

See all results for used cars for sale near 49505.

Industry observers note that we liked the 2027 Sienna more before we even pushed the start button. The Sienna’s upcoming steering wheel puts switches in more sensible locations; it’s much easier to operate on the fly, plus it looks better. The 2026 model’s tech feels a full step behind the 2027 model’s, with its analog gauge cluster (on the lower trims) and tiny info display, or the complete lack of USB-C ports. Thankfully, with the 2027 Sienna’s new tech comes a whole host of electrical-system changes, including a move to USB-C. Our tangled morass of a cable drawer thanks you, Toyota.

In addition to sprinkling better ports around the cabin, the Sienna’s upcoming updated tech also enhances the driving experience. The electronic power steering is lighter at lower road speeds, making around-town navigation slightly less onerous, and it also exhibits better on-center stability at highway speeds, again eliminating some tedium. The brakes also include a feature Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels to reduce body roll in cornering; after taking both Siennas to our 10Best evaluation loop, we can confirm that the revised Sienna does corner ever so slightly flatter, and you don’t even need to drive like a Car and Driver editor to feel the improvement.

As for the Sienna’s powertrain, we loved it in the latest generation of Lexus ES, and we very much enjoy it here as well. As Toyota promised, the sixth-gen hybrid brings noticeable improvements to noise, vibration, and harshness. In the 2026 model, the combustion engine sounds and feels coarser low in the rev range. In the 2027 model, the powertrain is both smoother and quieter, with an audible reduction in cabin noise (a change we’re excited to get the chance to confirm via testing at a later date). Simply put, driving the 2027 Sienna offers a more serene experience—for both driver and passengers—than you’d find in its predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that some changes incur massive cost penalties, but the 2027 Sienna doesn't ask too much extra off the top. It's estimated to come in around $44,500 for the base LE model with front-wheel drive. For context, the 2026 Sienna started at $42,915 for the base LE, rising to $60,305 for the top-spec Platinum; the slightly more rugged Woodland Edition was $53,695. Given just how much better the 2027 Sienna drives, we think it’s worth the higher cost of entry.

#110412. 'So No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way'

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (774 w)

'So No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way'

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (774 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Showing up for friends on their good days is easy.
  • Recent findings suggest that this month, Marsha Linehan, developer of DBT, died.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Showing up for friends on their good days is easy. You can celebrate their wins and enjoy their happiness. But being there, really being present for friends when they’re having a rough day or when they do dumb things, that can be more challenging. Our friend is upset, so they spend too much money, or they’re worried, so they pull out of something they had to do, or they’re angry, so they break things. How do we validate their emotions without endorsing their choices?

So, No One Told You Life Was Gonna Be This Way.

Recent findings suggest that this month, Marsha Linehan, developer of DBT, died. One of her many contributions to the psychology world was how to validate emotions with precision. She described six levels of how to validate emotions. The aim is to validate with the highest level possible, but different situations will require different levels. At all times, the goal is to help people notice that their emotion is valid and welcome, even if you don’t agree with the behavior that follows. Your friend doesn’t need a lecture after they’ve done something wrong; they want to feel emotionally understood.

It has been revealed that the most basic level is to simply stay awake and pay attention. I say "simply," but in these days of constant distractions, and phones and devices trying to hold our focus, even just being fully present can be a challenge. How can you show your friend that you’re really listening? You can use eye contact, nodding, asking questions, saying "uh-huh," and more.

In a recent development, the second level is accurate reflection. When you paraphrase back what they’ve remarked, you let them know that you’ve understood what they’re saying, especially the emotion they’re trying to communicate. Do this without criticism or advice, even if you don’t agree with everything they’ve said. Validation isn’t approval of behavior; it’s letting them know that their feelings are welcome.

It has been revealed that level three is reflecting the unarticulated parts. Let them know that you’ve understood even the aspects they haven’t explicitly told you. Name emotions that you’re guessing they’re probably feeling, e.g., "Oh my gosh, you must have been so hurt by him saying that." It doesn’t even matter if you guess the right emotion. If they reply, "Actually, I was more angry than sad," then you still have lots of emotion to validate.

Recent findings suggest that at the fourth level, you are validating using past history or biology. Letting your friend know that their behavior makes sense based on their life so far. Statements like "After all you’ve been through this year, I get why this would feel so painful" can put context to their uncomfortable emotions. Even if you would have felt differently in the same situation, you are able to validate their emotion because you understand that their road to this point has been different from yours.

Sources indicate that even more powerful than that is normalising the emotion. Letting your friend know that anyone in that situation would probably feel the same way. Saying things like "I get so upset when that happens," or "That’s something that worries me too," or "We all have moments like that." We can normalise the emotion, even when the behavior wasn’t something we agree with. We can understand that when we’re upset, we make choices that aren’t always the most helpful, and the emotion is still valid. Also, you can normalize their emotion without launching into your own similar story; if your friend is upset, they need you to listen to their pain.

Sources indicate that finally, the highest level of validation is radical genuineness. You listen to them describe their experiences, and you respond with genuine emotion. You're not patronising and saying "there, there." Instead, you are moved by their situation, and you care about them. This is demonstrated through words, body language, and emotion.

Validating your friends (or partner or family member) with the highest level of validation that feels appropriate for the situation is what will help you wholeheartedly be there for them when they’re broke, their job’s a joke, or their love life’s DOA.

Sources indicate that koerner, K. (2012). Doing dialectical behavior therapy: A practical guide. The Guilford Press.

Sources indicate that linehan, M. M. (1993). Cognitive-behavioral treatment of borderline personality disorder. Guilford Press.

In a recent development, linehan, M. M. (2020). Building a life worth living: A memoir. Random House.

Sources indicate that turn off reality TV and turn on the bald eagle cams. It’s all the drama you need.

When internet-famous bald eagle Shadow seemingly welcomed a mysterious latest female into his nest earlier this week, many fans have questioned the whereabouts of Kaydee. After the death of Shadow’s longtime partner Jackie in August, he had been spotted spending time with the 4-year-old banded female eagle named KD1 (later renamed Kaydee). It seemed like the eagles might head into mating season as a pair, but after the arrival of a new, large female, it’s unclear how the relationships will all shake out.

Since the appearance of the mystery female, nicknamed Major Beautiful Visitor or BBV by some fans, Kaydee has disappeared from view of Friends of Big Bear Valley (FOBBV)’s two cameras. She was last spotted by the cameras on November 14 in the Roost Tree, according to FOBBV. Despite concerns that she may be injured or had left the area, wildlife photographers have continued to document Kaydee’s presence near Big Bear Lake as recently as November 18.

According to recent reports, photographer Alla Shumko shared photos of Kaydee perched near Big Bear Lake on November 18. Kaydee’s double bands are visible as she observed a scuffle between younger eagles fighting over fish.

Mating season is well underway, so viewers of FOBBV’s 24/7 livecams have been watching closely for signs that Shadow has selected a latest partner. Shadow has worked with both Kaydee and the new eagle on nest maintenance and shared “beaky kisses” with each female, both signs of bonding in bald eagles. Bald eagle mating involves a bit of aerial acrobatics—copulating pairs can be seen in what’s called a “cartwheel display,” in which they lock talons in mid-air while tumbling down to the ground. Male eagles do not have an external phallus, so mating occurs via a touch of cloacas. Vocalizations can typically be heard during the act, which lasts about 7 to 12 seconds, according to Raptor Resource.

As this is nature, we humans can’t predict or influence who Shadow will pick as a latest partner. Or if he picks at all. All we can do is watch and wait and let nature take its course.

Electric Vehicles Now Make Up Nearly 1/3rd of Global New Car Sales: Study

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the conversion of the automotive industry over to electric vehicles, sold as a foregone conclusion by many car brands in the early 2020s, may have largely stalled out in America, but the picture is far different globally.
  • Recent findings suggest that and the global increase came despite falling sales in China.
  • Sources indicate that meanwhile, electric vehicle sales have declined in the United States this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the conversion of the automotive industry over to electric vehicles, sold as a foregone conclusion by many car brands in the early 2020s, may have largely stalled out in America, but the picture is far different globally. According to data from the Commonwealth Bank of Australia, EVs now account for 31 percent of all passenger vehicle sales.

Recent findings suggest that and the global increase came despite falling sales in China. The major driver of electric vehicle sales has been Europe; European EV sales have risen 37 percent year over year so far in 2026, climbing to 43 percent of the new vehicle sales market. CommBank data also demonstrated substantial growth rates in countries such as Brazil (EV sales up 164 percent, to a 13 percent market share) and India (EV sales up 76 percent, to a 9 percent market share). Even in Japan, where manufacturers have been notably EV-reticent, sales jumped 80 percent year-over-year to 5 percent of the market.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, electric vehicle sales have declined in the United States this year. According to Cox Automotive data, EV sales made up 6.4 percent of the new car market in Q3 of 2026, down from more than 10 percent in Q3 of 2025. Fuel prices have been elevated this year, but that has led Americans to gravitate toward hybrids rather than fully electric vehicles. Total electrified vehicles now account for nearly 25 percent of the American market.

Recent findings suggest that much of the decline has been a direct result of Trump administration policies. Last year, the U.S. eliminated a $7500 federal tax credit for electric cars, which—due to a commercial vehicle loophole—made them especially cheap for buyers to lease; the 10 percent share of sales in Q3 2025 came from a glut of sales as buyers rushed to take advantage of the tax credits before they expired. Congress is also considering imposing an annual federal tax on electric cars.

The Trump administration has also effectively eliminated enforcement of America’s CAFE standards, which would have effectively forced manufacturers to sell EVs to avoid hefty fines. American laws and tariffs also effectively prohibit importing affordable Chinese-made EVs, which have been a major reason behind the sales increase in Europe.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species.
  • “Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, noted in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement.
  • The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that less than 400 adult North Atlantic right whales (Eubalaena glacialis) still exist in the wild, making them one of the world’s most critically endangered species. Of those, 20 have officially received spiffy new names from conservationists at the New England Aquarium’s Anderson Cabot Center for Ocean Life. The researchers curate the annual North Atlantic Right Whale Catalog, and attach personable monikers to a select few baleen cetaceans in order to more easily monitor them. This year, it’s time to wave hello to Dodo, Volcano, and Dolly.

“Naming right whales is a fun and creative activity for our research community, but it also allows an opportunity to connect with the whales on an individual level,” Amy Warren, an aquarium scientific program officer and name project coordinator, noted in Anderson Cabot Center’s announcement. “It can be hard to relate to Catalog #5299, but a whale named Nibbles is bound to be memorable.”.

The 2026 inductees also include Grand Slam (Catalog #3991) and Slide (Catalog #4991). The sister whales have a mother named Fenway (Catalog #2791), who was also named in honor of the Boston Red Sox. Grand Slam earned her fresh name thanks to her three patches of raised tissue known as callosities that resemble the bases on a baseball field. Meanwhile, Slide received their name due to the curved scar on her back that recalls someone sliding through home plate. Other right whale names this year include Goose, Donegal, and even Gonzo for the beloved Muppet.

“Although the names are intended to help researchers at sea, they also give the general public a better understanding of the individual whales,” added Caroline Mowdy, a spokesperson for Whale and Dolphin Conservation (WDC).

Collaborators at the WDC also created some lighthearted, yearbook-esque biographies for each whale. For example, Dolly (Catalog #4191), whose callosity looks strikingly similar to the late, great country singer’s larger-than-life hair, apparently loves the song, “Jolene.” Then again, who doesn’t?

“We see these whales and their families grow each year,” said Mowdy. “Knowing them makes the tragedies even more tragic, but it also makes our determination to protect them even stronger.”.

On Monday, the North Atlantic Right Whale Consortium announced that there are roughly 382 North Atlantic right whales, representing a 1.8 percent drop in population size from the 2024 estimate. Their primary threats remain getting tangled in fishing line and vessel strikes.

In a recent development, however, even amid their struggles, the 2025–2026 right whale calving season saw the most calves born since 2009. A total of 24 calves were born, including a surprising late addition that was spotted in Canada in September.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’d be forgiven for not remembering PUBG: Black Budget, the extraction off-shoot of the original battle royale shooter, PUBG. Black Budget has been sort of floating around the internet for months, but Krafton never really committed to revealing core details about the game, or when players will actually get to play it.

This changes today, as the publisher - along with the game’s developer, PUBG Studios, have finally lifted the lid off the upcoming shooter.

Industry observers note that black Budget is described as a “tactical” extraction shooter. Squads of players infiltrate a mysterious island trapped in a time loop. There’s a bit of a STALKER element here with anomalies and various, unpredictable environmental shifts.

Coli, the island in question, hides a research facility that holds secrets and artefacts, which is what players will be attempting to extract. This is very much a PvPvE shooter, though PUBG Studios says the focus will be on exploration and discovery, rather than constant combat.

In a recent development, the game’s first set of closed alpha tests is set for December. The first takes place December 12-14, and another is scheduled for December 19-21. That’s six days across two weeks, with the test only being available on PC. Both sessions will be open to players in North America, Europe, and Asia.

According to recent reports, as it usually works with these sorts of tets on Steam, the game’s Steam page has a link where you can request access. If granted, you’ll be able to find the closed alpha in your library and download it when the time comes.

Though this is a closed test, Krafton confirmed that players will be able to capture and livestream their gameplay. In fact, watching content creators might be how you get access, as Black Budget is going to have a Twitch Drops event running alongside those sessions.

When I played Arc Raiders prior to its launch, I likened its tense and uncertain atmosphere to that of the early days of PUBG, so it’s going to be very interesting to see what actual PUBG does with the extraction shooter premise.

So far, it sounds like it’s going to be doing its own thing, leaning more into the adventure side of the subgenre, but we’ll have to see how it all shakes out when the tests start. Indeed, the BR-like constantly shrinking circle sounds like it could be a game-changing twist.

#110405. Why We Look Away: Examining Our Response to Homelessness

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1096 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Why We Look Away: Examining Our Response to Homelessness

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • “We do not see things as they are, we see things as we are." —Anaïs Nin.
  • Sources indicate that we see homeless individuals on street corners begging, with signs asking for help outside grocery stores, in bank kiosks trying to keep warm, and pushing carts with their belongings, to name just a few places.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

“We do not see things as they are, we see things as we are." —Anaïs Nin.

Sources indicate that we see homeless individuals on street corners begging, with signs asking for help outside grocery stores, in bank kiosks trying to keep warm, and pushing carts with their belongings, to name just a few places. We see people in line at soup kitchens or awaiting entrance to shelters. Those of us in the mental health field see more and hear more about homelessness than the usual person.

In a recent development, homelessness is often discussed in terms of economics, housing shortages, mental illness, and addiction. But there is an alternative dimensional way that we might examine this problem: the psychology behind our response to homelessness. What happens inside us when we encounter another person in need and in distress?

There are five different dimensions of our response to homelessness that I would like to discuss.

First, there is the discomfort of witnessing another person suffering or in need of help. There might be sadness, discomfort, helplessness, perhaps guilt for what we might have, and some revulsion. Witnessing another person’s suffering so openly tells us something about what we all experience at some point in our lives, which is human vulnerability. We depend on a sense of stability, security, and predictability in our lives. We have familiar routines, homes we return to, tasks we need to accomplish, friends who support us. Perhaps viewing another in such dire circumstances disrupts our own sense of permanence and predictability. We may look away, move on more swiftly, or stare surreptitiously.

Secondly, we may manage discomfort by creating a sort of psychological boundary between the homeless person and us. We might note that these individuals are different from us. Their circumstances, such as severe illness, lengthy unemployment, and exposure to trauma or domestic violence, are difficult to comprehend. This apparent distance might falsely reinforce the idea that our lives are secure. The greater the difference we create between ourselves and homeless people, the less humanity and humility we experience. On the other hand, erecting this boundary provides us with a sense of distance and difference.

Recent findings suggest that thirdly, there are social cues that we all respond to. If one sees others passing a homeless person sitting or standing on the street, we may believe that no response is necessary or that others will help. We look to others around us to determine how to behave. For example, if we arrive for a party and note that all people entering are kissing the host or hostess, we may be more likely to behave the same way. Follow the leader is a lesson we might have been taught that perhaps needs to be unlearned.

In a recent development, fourthly, perhaps one of the greatest barriers to understanding homelessness is our tendency to be judgmental and make assumptions about people who are homeless. We might make the mistake of assuming mental illness, laziness, or unwillingness to get a job, even if it is menial work. We may blame poor judgment or irresponsible decisions. It is a fundamental attribution error, which is the tendency to explain the behavior of another through personal characteristics rather than circumstances that might have befallen a person.

In a recent development, stigma creates a social barrier. Once we label someone, we stop seeing them as an individual and more as their label. Their history, personality, relationships, hopes, and dreams become inconsequential to the label we assign someone. For instance, I have often heard practitioners call someone schizophrenic rather than a person with schizophrenia.

The reality is that homelessness is a circumstance, not an identity.

Industry observers note that finally, when we are constantly exposed to the homelessness, war, poverty, and violence that are a routine part of our social media today, we may experience what can be best called compassion fatigue. When people feel overwhelmed by the number of problems they are exposed to daily and their inability to do anything about it, they simply turn away. It produces emotional numbing and avoidance. As we travel to and from work each day by walking or driving, or go to the same supermarket and pass the same person on the sidewalk, they, in essence, become part of the landscape of the route.

This same response occurs for caregivers of very ill persons, who might experience an emotional numbing or habituation.

Understanding these five psychological reactions—discomfort, distancing, social conformity, judgment, and compassion fatigue—gives us a way to think about homeless people and their impact on our behaviors.

Awareness is the first step toward choosing a different response. When someone becomes part of the landscape, we stop noticing them altogether. If instead we stop for a moment and examine our own discomfort rather than rushing past, perhaps we can change our responses, if we so choose. Our own unease likely comes from our own sense of vulnerability and lack of predictability in this world.

This small shift in framing can neutralize the fundamental attribution error and restore personal history to the person. Each person sitting on a sidewalk was once a child, has a birthday, had a family of origin, probably went to school somewhere, and had people in their lives who cared for them.

Sources indicate that breaking the spell of social cues requires a conscious choice. Making brief eye contact, offering a warm greeting, or simply nodding in recognition of another person’s presence counters the invisibility of living on the street or having to beg. It reaffirms their dignity. In some way or another, we all want to be noticed.

Addressing compassion fatigue demands a different balance. We cannot carry the weight of every global crisis or every unhoused person on our shoulders. There is a marked distinction between empathy—feeling someone else’s distress as our own—and compassion, which combines care with a desire to help in some way. When we shift from overwhelmed empathy to compassion, we move away from paralysis to practicality.

It has been revealed that returning to Anaïs Nin’s insight, the way we react to homelessness is ultimately a mirror. When we look away, we are often protecting our own illusion of control and permanence. When we choose to look closer—with humility, curiosity, and basic human kindness—we acknowledge another person’s struggle and reclaim their and our humanity. There is an inner person inside all of us.

GM Energy and WeaveGrid are launching a vehicle-to-grid (V2G) pilot that will let select Southern California Edison (SCE) customers send electricity from their EV batteries back to the grid. Eligible drivers could get more than $16,000 in help with equipment and installation, and earn money when the grid needs their power.

Industry observers note that GM says the pilot participants will be its first EV drivers in California to export power from their cars to their homes. Through the California Energy Commission, eligible customers in SCE’s Emergency Load Reduction Program can get up to $8,000 toward a GM Energy V2H system and up to $8,099 toward eligible installation costs, including connecting the system to the grid.

Chevy, GMC, and Cadillac EV drivers can use time-of-use energy management to take advantage of lower rates and may be paid for participating in eligible demand-response events. How much they save or earn depends on their rate proposal, electricity use, and participation.

GM already offers managed charging through 13 utilities, and each program varies by utility.

According to recent reports, an EV battery stores direct current (DC), and your house and the grid use alternating current (AC). GM’s current home backup system uses a wall-mounted inverter to convert the power. With AC bidirectional charging, the car’s onboard inverter does the job. Moving that work into the car could make the equipment on your garage wall simpler and cheaper to install.

Recent findings suggest that not in CA, but we use solar, time of use, and EVs to minimize our energy costs. We’re not feeding power back to the grid from our cars, but the combo of TOU, solar and EVs does allow us to reduce costs significantly. Solar covers all the expensive peak power, I have the cars start charging early enough to use any extra solar, and the rest is off peak at half cost.

GM is joining CharIN‘s North American AC V2G task force, which is working to align technical standards, equipment certification, and utility approval requirements. In Southern California, the pilot will give GM and its partners a look at how the process works for drivers, from signing up and getting the hardware installed to getting utility approval and sending power back.

#110403. Breaking: Newly introduced electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (804 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Newly introduced electric comb from China regrew nearly 100% of hair (in mice)

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results.
  • Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development states the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.
  • According to recent reports, created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A potentially revolutionary electronic comb is generating some pretty hair-raising results. The experimental comb has been used to successfully restore nearly all the hair in bald test subjects. But don’t chuck out that Rogaine just yet. The comb’s customers were mice with shaved backs.

Though the Detangle comb (named after the 2010 Disney film Tangled) hasn’t been tested on humans yet, the Chinese scientist behind its development states the eye-grabbing results on our distant genetic cousins suggest it could play a role in the neverending quest to keep those luscious locks just a hair longer.

According to recent reports, created by a team led by Beihang University in Beijing, the comb initially looks like the chunky plastic kind adorning typical pharmacy aisles. However, a closer look at its clear plastic handle reveals a green circuit board. Further down, one can see electrodes embedded in the comb’s teeth, which alternate between long and short. The team says that this height variance makes the comb’s pulsed electric field more than two and a half times stronger than it would be with evenly matched teeth.

The shorter teeth also contain two experimental genetic treatments. One boosts blood vessel growth around the hair follicles. The other treatment  blocks dihydrotestosterone (DHT), a hormone known to shrink follicles. The electric field generated by the comb temporarily opens up skin so the treatments can get inside, reaching up to nine times deeper into the follicle region than a conventional cream.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​.

According to recent reports, researchers performed a variety of tests on mice that had their backs shaved and were given testosterone to mimic pattern baldness. Over 28 days, the balding mice were treated with minoxidil or finasteride (the current standards for medical hair restoration), the comb’s electrical stimulation alone, and the comb combined with an experimental genetic treatment. Mice given finasteride regrew about 50 percent of their hair, while the ones on and minoxidil regrew 70 percent. Those numbers  honestly aren’t  too bad on their own, but the results were even better when Detangle got involved. Mice treated with the comb and both experimental treatments saw a staggering 97.85 percent hair regrowth. And all without having to book a flight to Turkey for a hair transplant.

“[T]hese results demonstrate that electrostimulation via the Detangle system promotes hair growth and follicle regeneration in a safe and effective manner,” the team wrote in their paper published earlier this month in the Nature Communications.

Industry observers note that the potential market for a hair regrowing comb is sizable to say the least. Detangle’’s creators say androgenetic alopecia, the scientific term for pattern baldness, affects 1.5 billion people worldwide. Some studies suggest up to 80 percent of men will experience pattern baldness, with  some populations seeing symptoms before the age of 40. Somewhere between one fifth and two fifths of women may also experience pattern hair thinning. And hair isn’t just hair. Social expectations and norms around hair partly explain why hair loss can carry psychological baggage.

In a recent development, scientists and hair care providers know this, of course. Toupees, tonics, and tinctures promising to reverse nature’s balding date back thousands of years. Today, the standard medical treatment usually involves topical minoxidil (the active ingredient in Rogaine) and oral finasteride. Minoxidil generally works, but results vary widely from person to person and it requires constant, ongoing application.

Finasteride is often far more effective, with long-term studies showing it can preserve hair in most men for at least a decade, but it also carries the risk for much more intense side effects. The drug (which saw a surge in popularity thanks to online, telehealth services) has been linked to decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. Some patients have also reported anxiety, depression, and suicidal thoughts. While the side effects are uncommon, the risk presented a potentially steep trade off for a fuller head of hair.

According to recent reports, those intrigued by the comb will unfortunately have to hold out quite a bit longer. The team says more research is needed before the device is tested on humans and, even then, there’s no guarantee the rodent results will translate. Testosterone-induced hair loss on a shaved mouse back is a far cry from human pattern baldness, which typically creeps in over years.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also worth emphasizing that the electric comb, memorable as it is, wasn’t solely responsible for the best results. The pair of experimental genetic treatments used in the study (called SRD5A2 siRNA and VEGFA plasmids) also need to be tested in humans to ensure they are safe and don’t come with unintended side effects of their own. Wig stores, it seems, will live to see another day.

The Moon-Prayer Night is the massive in-world festival, marking Dameselette's final night before she sets off for the moon. The latest patch, of course, introduces new playable characters, one with an interesting mechanic.

The events of this latest chapter take place following Rarcher of Solnari’s defeat. The victory has given way to the Moon-Prayer Night celebrations, which brings various stalls to the Nasha Town, alongside a new souvenir stamp book where you can record your memories.

All is not fine, however, as Alice and Nicole Reeyn come bearing some bad news about phantoms appearing across the Nod-Krai region at Teyvat's borders. There’s a mystery to be uncovered here, and your journey to do so won’t be a lonely one.

It has been revealed that the highly-anticipated Durin is at last the newly introduced playable character. A 5-Star Pyro Sword wielder, Durin can switch between two different forms: one lets him deal damage, while the other is best suited to supporting the team.

Durin was once a dragon, you see, who was later given a human body. This is why he’s able to switch forms. The more powerful, Abyssal-infused form can launch major attacks on single targets to boost his own Vaporize and Melt damage, while his support form reduces enemies’ Elemental Resistance and deals AoE Pyro damage.

Durin’s Story Quest will shed more light on that aspect of his life, and completing it earns you a reward for him. Speaking of quests, completing the Archon Quest will grant you 500 Primogems. As a member of Hexenzirkel, Durin and other characters can gain newly introduced powers when you complete more quests in Moon-Prayer Night.

Sources indicate that all characters connected to the Hexenzirkel can benefit from certain story quests tied to their abilities. This is a significant new addition, and will affect Venti, Klee, Albedo, Mona, Razor, Fischl, and Sucrose - all of whom can become Hexerei characters. This ties into the new Hexerei Secret Rite effect, which will trigger when two or more Hexerei characters are present. The effect boosts the entire party’s combat effectiveness.

The other new character in Luna 3 is Jahoda, a 4-Star Anemo Bow wielder who’s great at healing teammates and absorbing Elements, which she can then use to deal damage. The first phase of Luna 3 will feature Durin and Jahoda, alongside the return of Venti. The second phase sees no new character debuts, but does feature the return of Varesa and Xilonen.

There’s more to get excited about in Luna 3, even if you don’t feel like spending most of your time in Nod-Krai. The Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey event will take you back to Dragonspine, where you’ll find winter-theme minigames appropriate to an update cycle spanning December to January. This is how you can earn the 4-Star Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow, too.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, you can also look forward to the Miliastra Wonderland UGC module getting new updates. The Wonderland Resource Center is where creators can get and share resources through the editing tool.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Cincinnati Zoo’s most famous resident Fiona the hippo has died at age 9.

“We are in shock at the moment,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike mentioned in a statement. “We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn’t anymore. Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore. She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”.

Last week, a child’s knit hat entered her enclosure at the Cincinnati Zoo and the almost 10-year-old hippo ate it. Given her size, zookeepers initially thought she’d simply pass the hat, but it remained stuck in her digestive track. She had undergone a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope and multiple ultrasounds that showed intestinal bunching, indicating her body was trying and expel the hat. Caretakers have continued to give her fluids and sedate her when necessary for tests. Just yesterday, on November 18, the zoo shared a new approach in Fiona’s ongoing treatment: a vibration plate borrowed from a local Ohio horse farm. Fiona could be seen standing on the plate, vocalizing to caretakers.

Sources indicate that “Fiona was such a gift,” noted Cincinnati Zoo Executive Chair of the Board Thane Maynard. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And, she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”.

Industry observers note that fiona first captured the internet’s heart in 2017, when she was born six weeks premature. Baby hippos typically weigh about 100 pounds at birth, but tiny Fiona tipped the scales at a mere 29 pounds. She was the smallest known hippo to survive such a low birth weight. As she grew, Fiona took social media and the real world by storm: she photobombed an engagement shoot, had a local ice cream named in her honor, and even starred in her own reality-TV series appropriately called “The Fiona Show.”  Her surprise baby brother Fritz was born in 2022, after their mother’s birth control went “on the fritz.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NHL may not be a household name, but its all-upcoming, all-electric NTE240E ultra-class haul track could change that with a 240 ton payload, over 4.1 MWh of battery, advanced regenerative braking, and a world’s first double-gun MCS charging setup.

For the uninitiated, Inner Mongolia North Hauler Joint Stock Co., Ltd. (NHL) is a Chinese heavy equipment manufacturer specializing in the enormous rigid-frame haul trucks used in open-pit mining operations. Established in 1988, NHL has decades of experience building mining trucks for customers around the world, including some of the industry’s largest diesel-electric hybrids. The brand’s new NTE240E is different, representing a firm’s real push into battery-electric mining equipment, and it’s powering that push with some seriously ambitious technology.

According to recent reports, let’s start with the battery. The NTE240E packs an absolutely MASSIVE battery pack, with the highest-capacity versions offering up to 4,100 kWh (4.1 MWh) of onboard energy storage. Keeping that much battery topped off is no small task, which is why NHL developed an equally ambitious energy replenishment strategy supporting dual-gun MCS charging, allowing its town-sized battery to go from 20% to 90% in under an hour.

That means operators can take advantage of shift changes and scheduled rest breaks to top off the battery without sacrificing an entire work shift to charging – but even more impressive than the fact that all that juice can be crammed into so massive a battery in so little time is the fact that, according to NHL, it can be done at just 25°C (about 77°F).

Plugging in isn’t the only way the NTE240E drinks its juice. NHL’s upcoming dynamic power reception system uses overhead current collectors to supply electricity directly to the truck while it’s climbing loaded mine roads, allowing it to then “ride the brakes” for more energy all the way downhill.

In a recent development, the combined technologies allow NHL’s operators to keep the massive trucks moving without relying entirely on their onboard batteries. The result is a claimed 15% improvement in energy efficiency over the ultra-class industry average.

That efficiency turns into savings, which means the economics of running an NTE240E could be just as compelling as the emissions savings – and those are substantial. NHL notes each NTE240E can reduce harmful carbon emissions by more than 2,000 tons annually, even as it cuts operating costs by more than 60% compared to a comparably capable diesel.

Recent findings suggest that what’s more, because the big BEV’s electrical system eliminates the need for engine-related hardware like generators and the maintenance and overhaul costs associated with those components. Taken as a whole, the NHL seems to be a compelling offering … but that’s not for me to say. You guys are the experts – let us know what you think of the new NHL NTE240E, in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The first manual C8-gen Chevrolet Corvette is running and driving only a year after Tremec confirmed its upcoming TR-9060 six-speed manual transaxle, and Road & Track just got a chance to take it for a spin.
  • In a recent development, the car in question, built by Peitz Performance in Texas, is actually a race car, and it’s still in the early prototype phase.
  • It has been revealed that the basics are relatively straightforward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first manual C8-gen Chevrolet Corvette is running and driving only a year after Tremec confirmed its upcoming TR-9060 six-speed manual transaxle, and Road & Track just got a chance to take it for a spin.

In a recent development, the car in question, built by Peitz Performance in Texas, is actually a race car, and it’s still in the early prototype phase. In other words, my test is not representative of what a polished and optimized road car will feel like. But it was enough to prove that the concept works.

It has been revealed that the basics are relatively straightforward. Tremec engineered this latest six-speed transaxle to fit lots of different cars, from the C8 Corvette to McLarens and more. It’s for the aftermarket to play around with, as Chevy has made it clear the C8 won’t be getting a manual from the factory. Alex Peitz, the owner of Peitz Performance, had an existing relationship with Tremec, which is how he managed to get his hands on one of these transaxles before regular production of them begins. (Tremec notes it’s targeting July 2027 for initial sales to distributors.).

According to recent reports, already neck-deep in C8 builds, Peitz used his experience and—most importantly—3-D scans of the car. This head start helped him map out how he’d install the transmission, shift cables, clutch, and shifter before he even had the parts in hand. A heavily modified Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing clutch pedal is squeezed into the pedal box. There was some fear that the latest gearbox would interfere with the exhaust system, but that ended up not being an matter once it was installed. Of all the problems to solve, though, making the C8’s complicated and advanced electrical architecture talk nicely with the manual was the toughest challenge. It’s one Peitz admits he is still sorting out.

It has been revealed that on top of being version one of the manual C8 Corvette, Peitz’s car is a fully caged and built race car, with all the temperamental nature common to the breed. Unfortunately, when I arrived to drive it, the power steering and ABS had recently left the chat. With massive slicks mounted both front and rear, that made steering the car one hell of an arm workout. On top of that, the fixed bucket seat was, well, fixed. Peitz has longer legs than I do, and I was only just barely able to get the extremely heavy race clutch to the floor with the toe of my shoe extended as far as I could.

The good news is that the transmission itself seems to work without problem. Driving the C8, I felt instantly familiar with where each gear should be. There was no vagueness or sloppiness to be found. That remarked, what was missing was the affirmative thud I was expecting as each gear was fully selected. The weight of the throw action was oddly light for such a powerful and torquey car, although not offensively so. But these are preferences that should hopefully be tweaked later as the aftermarket fine-tunes the action of the gearchanges with bushings and shifter design.

Recent findings suggest that one thing every manualized C8 is set to struggle with is shifter placement. The car’s center console was never designed with a manual transmission in mind. It is too tall, and that presents a problem for ergonomics, as the latest shifter sits inherently higher than where you expect to find it. Depending on an individual driver’s height or arm length, it may work fine, but my arm felt far too high in the air as I grabbed each gear. A shorter shifter might help, but only by making the problem less noticeable as opposed to fixing it entirely.

Rev matching was remarkably easy, although the pedal placement meant I wasn’t able to heel-and-toe. Auto rev matching will be possible, Peitz claims, and while the demonstrator doesn’t have it now, it will be an option for those who want to convert their cars in the future. And this early pedal arrangement will surely evolve as Peitz and other shops work up more polished solutions.

Sources indicate that one of the promising aspects that should not change is the gearing. I tested the car at Michigan’s newest racetrack, Motorsports Gateway, and found myself constantly shifting thanks to the relative shortness of the ratios. This is definitely a good thing; you choose a manual for the pleasure of changing gears. Porsche 718 owners know the curse of especially long gears well—if you can go over 80 mph in second gear, you end up rarely actually needing to shift on a twisting road. That won’t be the case for a C8 with the Tremec, because like with the eight-speed Tremec dual-clutch in the factory C8, you are going to stay busy stirring the pot.

Beyond that, at this stage, I can’t say too much about how a roadgoing C8 manual will be, but Peitz gets credit for doing the hard yards of proving it is indeed possible to get three pedals into the mid-engined Corvette. Tremec says it plans on installing its transmission in a test car of its own next year, and that will be a bone-stock production C8. We’ll be champing at the bit to get behind the wheel of that one when it ultimately happens. But Peitz Performance deserves the credit for getting here first. The manual Corvette is back!

In a recent development, some mid-cycle updates focus on aesthetics, bringing some newly introduced style (and hopefully some new eyes) to a slightly older product. The 2027 Toyota Sienna skipped those pleasantries and focused on the meat and potatoes: its hybrid powertrain.

Industry observers note that the 2027 Toyota Sienna looks no different—unless you count the Cypress paint color, which was dropped and swapped with Storm Cloud—but it’s what’s lying under the body that matters more here. The Sienna adopts Toyota’s sixth-generation hybrid powertrain, which first arrived in the upscale Lexus ES Hybrid. A new electric motor packs more efficient silicon-carbide conductors, and it pairs with a 1.15-kWh battery that ditches the old nickel-metal hydride chemistry in favor of lithium-ion. In addition, there’s a whole new electrical platform underpinning it all, with new ECUs and software to manage everything.

See all results for new 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 94043.

Combine all that with a 2.5-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine that has been retuned for quieter low-speed operation, and you have a Toyota Sienna that produces a whopping six horsepower more than before, rising from 245 horses to 251. Engine torque is unchanged at 176 pound-feet, and Toyota did not specify e-motor torque. That small power bump is enough to affect its acceleration: Toyota estimates a 7.5-second sprint to 60 mph in front-wheel-drive Sienna variants, rising to 7.6 seconds with AWD. That’s 0.3 or 0.4 second quicker than before, respectively.

Even with that bump in speed, Toyota claims improved fuel economy in the 2027 Sienna, to the tune of +3 mpg in the city for FWD models and +4 mpg in the city for AWD models. Combined estimates rise 1 or 2 mpg. For context, the 2026 model is EPA estimated at 36 mpg city/36 highway/36 combined for the front-driver, and 35/36/35 for the AWD.

There have also been some tweaks to other electrical-adjacent components. The electronic power steering promises less effort at low speeds, while improving on-center feel at highway speeds. That adjustment includes a latest steering-wheel layout that will eventually migrate to other sixth-gen-equipped hybrids. Toyota also fiddled with its brake electronics, resulting in less pedal effort and a smoother blend between regen and friction braking. The Sienna also includes something Toyota calls Vehicle Braking Posture Control, which applies braking to individual wheels with the aim to reduce body roll during cornering.

In a recent development, creature comforts get some upgrades as well. A 12.3-inch infotainment screen is now standard across the lineup (the LE grade ditches its 8.0-incher), as is a 12.3-inch gauge cluster (LE and XLE get this instead of the old 7.0-inch getup). There’s newly introduced LED cabin lighting, plus a revised rear-seat entertainment system that now features native apps on a new touchscreen. Upgraded dashboard sound abatement promises to lower the cabin volume by one decibel.

See all results for fresh 2027 Toyota Sienna for sale near 94043.

According to recent reports, toyota also slimmed down the Sienna’s trims for 2027. The Limited grade has been dropped in favor of adding more features to the sporty XSE variant, which rises to become the trim underneath the Platinum. As a result, the 2027 Sienna XSE picks up niceties like ventilated front seats with memory, a panoramic-view monitor, and a head-up display. The rugged Woodland Edition trim also picks up the surround-view tech. The upgraded rear-seat entertainment is available on the Woodland, XSE, and Platinum trims.

It has been revealed that the 2027 Toyota Sienna reaches dealerships in early—you guessed it—2027. Pricing starts around $44,500 for the front-wheel-drive LE base trim, which represents a price bump of less than $2000 over a base 2026 Sienna. Not too shabby for a whole newly introduced generation of powertrain.

#110395. The Unapologetic Ferocity of Activism

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (604 w)

The Unapologetic Ferocity of Activism

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan.
  • In the summer of 1981, my family was returning from a meal in Chinatown.
  • In a recent development, “What a shame,” she mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Abigail Fagan.

In the summer of 1981, my family was returning from a meal in Chinatown. I was wedged between my two older sisters in the back seat of my mother’s mint-green Cadillac when my eldest sister, Maria, jutted her chin toward the window.

In a recent development, “What a shame,” she mentioned. “They’re all gonna die.”.

Along the West Side Highway in the West Village, throngs of gorgeous, sinewy men posed in the late-afternoon light.

It was a startling thing to hear.

On July 3, 1981, the Newly introduced York Times had published its first story about the disease that would become known as AIDS. Most of the country hadn’t heard of it. President Ronald Reagan wouldn't publicly mention AIDS until September 1985, and by then thousands of Americans had already died.

In a recent development, I was 13 years old, and I didn’t yet have a word for what I was. Certainly, what those men represented was an abomination to my parents. But I understood, in the wordless way that children understand the things that frighten them most, that the virus killing those men might one day kill me too.

For years, Maria’s words haunted me.

According to recent reports, A decade later, in September 1991, Larry Kramer stood up at an ACT UP meeting in Fresh York and screamed that we were in the middle of a plague. By the end of that year, the epidemic had claimed more than 133,000 American lives. The 2012 documentary How to Survive a Plague captures the moment, and 35 years on, I can still hear Kramer’s banshee cry.

Then came 1996 and HAART (Highly Active Antiretroviral Therapy), which combined multiple antiretroviral drugs from different classes into a single regimen. For the first time, an HIV diagnosis was no longer a death sentence. In the years that followed, people living with HIV who maintained an undetectable viral load could expect a near-normal lifespan.

By the time I began working directly with HIV activists in 2015, HIV was considered a chronic, treatable condition. I assumed the dread I had carried since childhood belonged to another era and that young gay men today didn't live with it as I had.

Then I sat around a table with some of the leading HIV activists to discuss a upcoming clinical trial. I came in expecting to collect insights I would turn into a tactical proposal. Instead, the discussion turned into a shouting match. "The problem isn't the medicine," one activist mentioned, slamming his hand on the table. "It's how much it costs.".

Recent findings suggest that everyone turned to me, the pharmaceutical representative in the room. Weren't we on the same side?

Recent findings suggest that it took me longer than I’d like to admit to understand what I had walked into. Many of those activists had been fighting for their lives for their entire adult lives. They had buried partners and friends, watched their government turn a blind eye, and learned that politeness got people killed.

On December 1, we observe World AIDS Day to raise awareness, support people living with HIV, and remember those we lost. For me, it’s a day to remember those activists, whom I came to admire as much as I once feared them. Around that conference table, I learned what ACT UP had been shouting since 1987: Silence = Death.

Their ferocity was never the problem. It’s the reason many people are still here.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even if you don’t care about the rivalries between the top multiplayer first-person shooters series, it’s hard to ignore how much EA wanted to stick it to Call of Duty this year with Battlefield 6.

Activision saw that coming early enough that it ran multiple free weekends around major moments for EA’s game, including its launch, seemingly in an effort to capture some of those players and keep them away from BF6.

Both Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 have now launched, and though exact sales figures may never be detrmined (though EA did announce 7 million sold in the first week), it’s very clear at this point from every metric we can see that BF6 came out on top this year.

Recent findings suggest that the recent Black Ops 7 launch clearly hasn’t made many people happy, so just like Activision made Black Ops 6 free to play at BF6’s launch, EA has now done the same with its own game. The Battlefield 6 free trial, which was confirmed last week, is just an hour away at the time of this writing.

This is the first trial for the core game, and it arrives some six weeks after Battlefield 6 officialy launched, and four weeks following the release of the free-to-play Battlefield Redsec, which has battle royale and other components.

Beyond all the drama surrounding the two rival shooter franchises, the Battlefield 6 trial is itself pretty straightfoward, and is notably nowhere near as genrous as some of the Call of Duty ones we’ve seen recently.

According to recent reports, the trial goes live today at 4am PT, 7am ET, 12pm GMT across all platforms, and will be available for a week; ending Tuesday, December 2. It includes three core maps: Siege of Cairo, Eastwood, and Blackwell Fields.

According to recent reports, players will have access to four game modes, played on different versions of the same maps. Conquest, Breakthrough, Sabotage, and Team Deathmatch will all be available to choose from, and there don’t appear to be any level or XP limits in the trial.

Unfortunatley, just as the free trial was about to go live, the game got hit with a major matchmaking outage that took down all matchmaking in the core game, leaving Redsec unaffected.

Hopefully EA can resolve this issue before the trial officially kicks off.
