Max Verstappen and George Russell start side by side on the front row for the Las Vegas Grand Prix Saturday evening, thanks to a five-place grid penalty for pole-sitter and world champion Kimi Antonelli.

With this front row, there is no love lost over their careers and, more specifically, this weekend, as Russell enters the race upset, with a first step in following the clash between the two and FP3, in which Russell rebounded to top the time charts with a time of 1:34.805.

In FP3, Verstappen passed Russell and, in the next corner, braked hard, forcing the Mercedes driver to run off the racing line and towards the barrier in an evasive maneuver. Following the brake, the two banged wheels in a session without consequence. After the light collision, Verstappen flipped off Russell on the next straight. The drivers were called in front of the stewards, and Verstappen was given a warning after being found to have made an “unpredictable change of direction under braking.”.

Sources indicate that this was the third time during FP3 that Verstappen pulled such a move, as he was already under investigation for doing the same to the Alpine of Franco Colapinto and the McLaren of Lando Norris. Russell’s woes with Verstappen’s move this week is that he finds that the four-time champion has a pattern of behavior that screws over those he’s competing against. In this case overtaking at the start of a practice lap.

With FP3 being the only dry practice sessions of the weekend, emotions were elevated as drivers were pressed to figure out how the new car works on the coldest street circuit of the year.

Recent findings suggest that “There’s nothing in the rules that states you cannot overtake someone who is starting a lap but you’re screwing this person over,” Russell stated post race to sky sports Italia. “He does this week in and week out with many drivers and everyone accepts it.

“I’m not just going to accept somebody to screw me over like this and walk around like they’re bigger and better than everyone else. Somebody’s got to stand up to this guy.”.

When the comments were shared with Verstappen, he brushed them off, saying he wasn’t going to waste his time on the comments before adding that in racing there are no gentleman’s agreements.

“I've never heard of a gentleman’s agreement in my life, Verstappen stated.

Mercedes Team Principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports that, with his driver and his Red Bull advisory on the front row, we should expect cinema if they go for the same line into the opening corner of the Grand Prix tonight.

“If they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching,” Wolff stated.

This is the first time this year that the two start next to each other on the front row and the ninth across their careers.

#110364. Industry News: Direct Your Gratitude to a Person

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (696 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Direct Your Gratitude to a Person

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (696 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • As someone who is not naturally grateful, I dread hearing these words at Thanksgiving meals:.
  • “Can we go around the table and share what we are thankful for?”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

As someone who is not naturally grateful, I dread hearing these words at Thanksgiving meals:.

“Can we go around the table and share what we are thankful for?”.

People’s responses to this question generally follow the format, “I am grateful/thankful for __________.” I am grateful for good health. I am thankful for a recent promotion. I am grateful for the breathtaking nature around me. Some people might simply declare, “I am just so thankful,” without citing any reason.

Recent findings suggest that the sentiment captured in these responses is a feeling of gratitude. Maybe you know folks who are bursting with thankfulness and will express feeling grateful at every opportunity. Maybe you are that person.

It has been revealed that this kind of gratitude can be described as inward-facing. That is, what is expressed as thankfulness tends to amplify various aspects of the self by naming the things that are going well in one’s life.

It has been revealed that feeling grateful (and trying to increase that emotion) is one way to reap the benefits of gratitude for mental health. But it is not the only way. Outward-facing gratitude, one that is concerned with delivering a message of thanks to a specific target or recipient, should also be a part of how we practice gratitude. In the eagerness to feel gratitude within us, perhaps we have neglected action-oriented gratitude, one that directs thankfulness to a target outside of us. We need to address the imbalance.

In a recent development, as a bilingual person, I find it helpful to reflect on the contrast between Korean and English in the way thankfulness is expressed. In Korea, “thank you” (감사합니다 [gamsahamnida]) is reserved for when there is a clear interpersonal target. More to the point, it is unnatural to say “I feel grateful” in the Korean language; I mean, you could translate it literally, but the average Korean will find the phrasing awkward, as the expression of gratitude in Korean almost always identifies an interpersonal target.

Industry observers note that in the individualistic culture that is the U.S., we are prone to elevating feelings, such as the affective component of gratitude. But we need to balance the affective with the behavioral when it comes to how gratitude is understood. We need to look more outside of ourselves to affirm that person who demonstrated unexpected generosity and kindness. And verbal expressions of gratitude to someone need not be dependent on feeling grateful on the inside—if a colleague surprised me with my favorite coffee, hopefully I am moved by their generosity and therefore will say thank you; but even if my heart is not filled with gratitude in that moment for various reasons, I nonetheless have a social responsibility, an interpersonal obligation, to say gamsahamnida to that person.

It has been revealed that my research team interviewed individuals with chronic pain and their experiences with gratitude. All of the interviewees noted, in effect, that they genuinely struggle with gratitude when the chronic pain and its related adverse consequences become too intense (who can blame them?). At the same time, these individuals clearly described the kind and generous actions of another person as sources of their gratitude. A courageous doctor who tried a latest intervention that ended up working. A stranger who came to the rescue in an emergency situation. A supportive partner who heroically took on more responsibilities around the house.

In a recent development, in this holiday season and beyond, by all means, feel grateful. Name all the ways that you are thankful for the blessings in your life. But even while you look toward yourself in search of reasons to feel grateful, also be intentional about looking outward in recognizing the individuals who have shown extra kindness to you, sacrificed for you, or given generously to you.

And with each verbal expression of thanks to another person, with each handwritten or typed thank-you note delivered to another human being, you might find yourself feeling a bit more grateful.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that resilience and perseverance was on full display in Alaska this summer. The park rangers at Tongass National Forest in the southeastern corner of the state spotted an unnamed black bear (Ursus americanus) with a broken arm. Even with this injury, the tough bear still managed to catch the fish running through Anan Creek. For this grit, the rangers awarded the bear with the 2026 Grin & Bear It Award.

“We don’t know how the injury happened, but we’re impressed by the bear’s resilience,” the rangers write. “In other wild places the injury may have been a death sentence, but the abundance of Anan gives this bear a chance.”.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

According to recent reports, the largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area also includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and plenty of bears. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

Industry observers note that according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears like the one with the broken arm and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their portly counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own behaviors and quirks.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The FIA began the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend by announcing that all manufacturers have agreed to the framework to bring turbocharged V8 engines back to F1 and move away from the current V6 turbo.

This move has long been expected, with hopes that it will make engine building easier and cheaper while bringing back the sound that motorsport fans deeply miss.

The sound of the V8 engines was a rally cry for fans and has been sorely missed by audiences worldwide.

The F1 engine manufacturers agreed to a rough-out overarching plan to move to a 2.1-liter turbocharged V8 from 2030 onwards, with a lower charge of electrical power reducing the hybrid output from 350kW to 200kW, a decrease of nearly 56 percent.

The FIA revealed that ‘The plan is to marry the V8 power unit to a chassis which will also be lighter, more agile and placing greater emphasis on driver skill and close racing.”.

With everyone in agreement, PU manufacturers will start to jockey between improving the new car entering a sophomore season of new regulations and game planning for the major change coming just three seasons down the line.

It’s been 13 years since manufacturers last built a V8 engine for F1.

Sources indicate that “This agreement marks a significant milestone in shaping the future of Formula 1,” FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem mentioned. “From the outset, I have been clear in my ambition to deliver a sport that is more competitive and more exciting for our fans, while remaining at the forefront of innovation and sustainability.

Sources indicate that “The return of V8 engines represents an opportunity to reconnect with the DNA of this Championship, bringing back the sound, emotion and pure racing that is loved worldwide. Our vision is clear, lighter, simpler and more affordable cars that put driver skill at the heart of the competition.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road.
  • Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.
  • According to recent reports, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A retired EV battery can still have years of use left in it when it’s taken off the road. Moment Energy’s latest Nova battery storage system puts those packs to work on commercial sites. And when a pack wears out, it can be swapped without pulling out the whole system.

Nova was unveiled at RE+ in Las Vegas this week, and it’s already in production at Megafactory 1, the battery-repurposing plant that Moment Energy opened in the Vancouver area in June.

According to recent reports, each Nova unit delivers 500 kilowatt-hours (kWh) of energy and 200 kilowatts (kW) of power. It has a 2.94 m by 1.80 m (9.7 x 5.9 ft) footprint, and units can be linked together for projects in the tens of megawatt-hours. A site could charge the batteries when electricity is cheaper or when its solar panels are producing more than it needs, then draw on that power when demand spikes or the grid goes down.

Nova can use packs from different EV models, even when those packs have aged at different rates. Moment’s battery management software tracks how each pack is doing. As packs wear out, the company can replace them while leaving the enclosure and concrete pad in place. Moment says its pack replacement service could keep a system in service for more than 20 years.

It has been revealed that “We see a future where reengineered EV batteries become essential infrastructure for powering businesses and onshoring manufacturing and supply chains. Nova brings that vision to life, combining safety, engineering, and North American manufacturing to deploy the safest and highest-performance batteries ever made: EV batteries to supercharge our aging grid,” remarked Edward Chiang, co-founder and CEO of Moment Energy.

It has been revealed that moment Energy indicates Nova is the first storage system built from retired EV batteries to earn both UL 1973 certification for the batteries and UL 9540 certification for the complete system. It was also tested under UL 9540A, which looks at how a battery fire can spread. The factory itself is certified under UL 1974, which covers how used batteries are assessed and graded for reuse.

That matters for businesses with limited space. Nova is designed to sit outdoors alongside the buildings it serves. It uses liquid cooling, detects smoke, heat, and flammable gases, and is rated to operate from −13F to 122F (−25C to 50C).

Moment Energy also says an independent review found that Nova meets US federal sourcing restrictions tied to the clean electricity investment tax credit. Those rules are one part of determining whether a project qualifies for the credit.

Orders are open, and Moment Energy expects the first units to ship in Q1 2027 for deployments across North America.

Breaking: 1 in 3 Infants Diagnosed With Peanut Allergy May Not Have the Condition

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.
  • According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.
  • However, upcoming research published in the November 2026 issue of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.

According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.

However, upcoming research published in the November 2026 issue of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.

In fact, having a history of reacting to peanuts and positive allergy testing on their own may not be sufficient to diagnose a peanut allergy for many infants.

The study’s authors suggest that a threshold oral food challenge — in which the child is given increasing amounts of the suspected food allergen under medical supervision to look for an allergic reaction — should be routinely considered to help confirm peanut allergy.

This additional testing could safely prevent children who are not allergic to peanuts from undergoing unnecessary treatment with oral immunotherapy.

It could also spare families from burdensome food restrictions and allergy precautions.

The researchers’ goal was to evaluate the accuracy and safety of the Allergy Development to an Accelerated Path to Tolerance (ADAPT) peanut oral immunotherapy program, which was established in 2024 at 10 public children’s hospitals across Australia.

This program provides a standardized approach to evaluating and treating infants with suspected peanut allergies.

The study included infants who had experienced a mild to moderate reaction to peanut before 12 months of age and had evidence of peanut sensitization through allergy testing.

Researchers reviewed medical records to examine how accurately the program’s approach identified peanut allergies and whether it could safely guide treatment.

A key part of the evaluation was a threshold oral food challenge. The challenge involved up to seven doses, ranging from 15 to 1,300 milligrams of peanut protein.

Medical teams monitored the infants for reactions and provided treatment when necessary.

In a recent development, researchers reviewed records from April 2024 through October 2025. During that period, 1,275 infants were assessed through the program, and 778 underwent an oral food challenge.

The researchers also examined allergy test results and whether infants who reacted during the challenges could begin oral immunotherapy at an appropriate starting dose.

At the time of the oral food challenge, the infants had a median age of 13 months.

Of the 778 infants who underwent an oral food challenge, 507 (65.2%) had an allergic reaction.

However, 271 (34.8%) did not react to peanut during the supervised test, despite having a history of a previous reaction and positive allergy test results.

These findings suggest that relying on medical history and allergy tests alone may lead some infants to be labeled with a peanut allergy when they can actually tolerate the food.

Industry observers note that among the infants who reacted during the challenges, 61 experienced anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure. This represented 12% of infants with a positive challenge and 7.8% of all infants who underwent testing. Medical teams safely managed these severe allergic reactions.

Researchers also found that infants who reacted to peanut generally had higher skin prick test results and Ara h 2-specific IgE levels than those who did not react.

However, these test results did not reliably indicate how much peanut would trigger a reaction or how severe that reaction would be.

Of the 394 infants who began peanut oral immunotherapy, 384 (97.5%) successfully started treatment at a dose below the amount that had triggered a reaction during their food challenge.

The researchers say these findings support considering supervised oral food challenges to confirm suspected peanut allergies before starting treatment or recommending long-term avoidance.

Erin Banta, MD, a board certified allergist and immunologist who treats both children and adults at Latitude Food Allergy Care in Great Neck, New York, stated these findings are significant because they provide evidence for early use of oral food challenges in infants with peanut reactions.

“In those with mild-moderate prior reactions to peanut, early oral food challenge may allow for either delabeling of food allergy (in 1/3 of the patients in this study) or diagnosis of food allergy,” she told Healthline.

Banta, who wasn’t involved in the study, added that early delabeling takes a significant burden off the patient and their family.

“On the other hand,” she explained, “early diagnosis allows for early initiation of treatment with oral immunotherapy at a time in the patient’s life associated with the greatest success rates.”.

Banta further noted that the study offers different pathways for oral immunotherapy based on the patient’s reaction threshold. This means that some patients may be able to complete treatment more promptly due to their individual threshold dose.

Lindsey Forstie, FNP, a family nurse practitioner with clinical training and experience in allergy and asthma care at Carefree Allergy in Phoenix, AZ, added that while further evaluation may be needed to confirm a peanut allergy diagnosis, it’s notable for parents not to try introducing peanuts at home.

“Instead, they should speak with their pediatrician or allergist about appropriate testing and whether a supervised food challenge is safe and necessary,” she mentioned.

According to Forstie, who was also not part of the study, the goal is to avoid unnecessary food restrictions while also keeping children safe.

“The key message is that not every positive allergy test means a child has a food allergy,” she told Healthline. “Accurate diagnosis helps protect children while allowing those who are not allergic to enjoy a more normal, less restrictive diet.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield Studios is seemingly trying something different with Battlefield 6’s next patch, which everyone assumed would be a standard, mid-season enhancement not intended to change the game significantly.

However, it appears that it may bring more to the game than we realised, enough that the developer sees it as an excuse to bring back the pre-launch Battlefield Labs testing initiative.

Industry observers note that the December 9 patch kicks off the final phase of the game’s first season, which is set to take the game through the holidays and into the new year. We’ve known about its content for a while, and it’s definitely the lightest, compared to the two previous phases.

Battlefield Studios announced a host of fresh changes that will be included in the same patch, which are apparently significant enough to require player testing. The developer is reviving Battlefield Labs to help it do so, but only for three two-hour sessions, split across the game’s three main server regions (EU, NA, APAC).

All tests are scheduled for today, December 2, and they remain under NDA. Battlefield Labs is also sticking with PC as its chosen platform yet again, though you will be able to join through Steam this time, alongside the EA app.

Industry observers note that the focus of the test will be on three key areas that the December 9 patch will be touching. First, there’s footstep audio, an issue that was really brought into focus with the launch of Redsec Battle Royale. You can expect to hear enemy footsteps from farther away, and intuitively know the type of surface they’re moving on.

Recent findings suggest that the patch also brings another pass to hit registration and netcode, which BF Studios indicates should improve responsiveness in close-quarter situations. Finally, there are broader changes to other combat areas that the announcement didn’t elaborate on.

All testing will take place on Eastwood, and Operation Firestorm, rotating between Conquest, and Escalation.

Recent findings suggest that going forward, Battlefield Studios noted to expect Labs to be open to more players, and for the process itself to be smoother. The developer wants to have faster turnaround times, after all, so that the initiative can test smaller changes and be more responsive to player feedback.

According to recent reports, some of the more involved, future sessions will include experiments with map layout changes and various other non-standard compositions of player and vehicle numbers. Of course, you can also expect newly introduced maps and modes to be tested in Labs, similar to how the CTE was used in Battlefield 4’s long life.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the fresh-for-2026 Ferrari 296 Speciale is a sharper, faster, and more track-oriented variant of the brand’s V-6 supercar—but that doesn’t mean it is the only high-performance variant of the car that Ferrari will build. In a somewhat surprising break from recent tradition, Ferrari is also going to make a Challenge Stradale variant of the 296 to sell alongside the Speciale.

According to recent reports, as the name suggests, the Challenge Stradale is a road-going variant of the 296 that shares a lot in common with the race car currently used in various Ferrari Challenge series. Specifically, its aerodynamic elements are strikingly similar to the new 296 Challenge Evo, which was revealed alongside the new road car on November 21. The massive rear wing, front dive planes, and aggressive rear splitter are all extremely similar to design elements seen on that race car.

Recent findings suggest that those components combine to create a massive 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 miles per hour, an increase of 72 percent over the 296 GTB that won Road & Track Performance Car of the Year in 2024. Downforce is also up 401 lbs at that speed on the 296 Speciale, an increase of 29 percent.

The removal of the hybrid system means a reduction in power, dropping from a combined system output of 819 horsepower in the 296 GTB to an engine-only output of 670 hp in the Challenge Stradale. The simplified powertrain and stripped out interior mean serious reductions in weight to match, though; the Challenge Stradale is 309 lbs lighter than the GTB and 176 lbs lighter than the Speciale.

In a recent development, does the reduction in weight and increase in downforce make the 296 Challenge Stradale faster than the hybrid 296 Speciale already on the market? Not necessarily. Ferrari claims the Challenge Stradale is half a second a lap faster at its Fiorano test track, but marginally slower at a high-speed circuit like Monza. The more powerful Speciale should be quicker on other tracks with the on-throttle time necessary to allow the hybrid to stretch its legs, while the lighter Challenge Stradale should have the advantage on more technical circuits with more off-throttle time.

In a recent development, the other major differentiation between the Speciale and the Challenge Stradale is availability. While that other high-end 296 variant was a limited-run model, Ferrari stresses that the Challenge Stradale is a part of its regular lineup, and should be more available to buyers. It remains a Ferrari, so the market is unlikely to be flooded with 296s with massive wings in the years to come, but by supercar standards, it should be relatively attainable.

Ferrari has not yet unveiled a price for the American market, but the brand says that it should start at the equivalent of just under $320,000 in Italy, including value-added tax. Prices in one region do not necessarily translate directly to another, but that number would leave the 296 Challenge Stradale in the general range of the similarly track-focused likes of Porsche’s 911 GT3 RS and Ford’s Mustang GTD.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD is preparing to launch a upcoming flagship MPV soon after previewing the large people mover for the first time.

We knew it was coming soon after images of the camouflaged multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) began flooding the internet last month.

Zhang Zhuo, general manager of BYD’s Ocean sales division, confirmed the fresh flagship MPV is coming soon.

“A newly introduced creation for the times, born for the family,” Zhuo mentioned after posting a preview of it for the first time on his Weibo account on Friday.

According to recent reports, the latest flagship Ocean MPV is “coming soon,” according to Zhuo, but he didn’t reveal a specific debut date. He previously mentioned the manufacturer expects to launch its first MPV under the Ocean lineup by the end of 2026, so local reports suggest it will make an official debut next week at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto show, which kicks off on November 27.

Although it’s blurred, the preview highlights a similar shape and size to the recent spy images, with a roof-mounted LiDAR and traditional pull-style door handles.

It doesn’t appear to look much like the futuristic Ocean-V concept BYD unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show earlier this year, a preview of its first MPV under the Ocean series.

The concept featured a sliding center display screen and two different modes: Camping and Movie. In camping mode, the seats either fold flat to create a bed or swivel to face each other.

In Movie mode, the vehicle transforms into a private mobile theater with a large display screen that flips out of the dashboard.

While it may not have some of the more extravagant elements from the concept, the Ocean MPV is expected to be “flagship-worthy,” if you will, with BYD’s latest tech and other premium features like zero-gravity seats and plenty of digital screens.

The Ocean-V’s innovations “will gradually make their way into mass-production vehicles,” BYD remarked earlier this year.

BYD has yet to announce any details, but the flagship Ocean MPV is expected to be about the size of the Xia, a large plug-in hybrid minivan sold under its Dynasty lineup.

The BYD Xia measures 5,145 mm long, 1,970 mm wide, and 1,805 mm tall, with a 3,045 mm wheelbase.

Like the Xia, the Ocean MPV is expected to use BYD’s latest-generation DM-i plug-in hybrid system with a 1.5L engine and a 200 kW electric motor.

It has been revealed that the Xia starts at 249,800 yuan ($37,500) in China. It’s available with two BYD Blade LFP battery packs: 20.4 kWh and 36.6 kWh, providing pure electric CLTC ranges of 100 km (62 miles) and 218 km (135 miles). On a full tank of gas and full charge, the plug-in people mover offers a combined CLTC range of 1,163 km (722 miles).

Industry observers note that BYD also sells the flagship Denza D9 MPV under its luxury sub-brand. With the Denza D9 starting above 300,000 yuan and the Xia at around 250,000 yuan, the Ocean MPV is expected to fill the gap.

Zhuo said to stay tuned for more coming soon, so check back for updates.

#110354. Industry News: The Worst Time to Open ChatGPT Is Right After a Fight

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (757 w)

Industry News: The Worst Time to Open ChatGPT Is Right After a Fight

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • According to recent reports, when I teach about how people use AI for emotional support, I run a live demo using ChatGPT.
  • Sources indicate that AI is not a fixed thing the way an app is.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

According to recent reports, when I teach about how people use AI for emotional support, I run a live demo using ChatGPT. One prompt I use every time is "I'm having a panic attack on a plane, can you help?" It is a good example of how AI handles very specific requests from people (and usually handles them well). The challenge is that ChatGPT, like all AIs, responds differently every single time. Even with the same exact prompt, I am sometimes caught off guard by how different the response is.

Sources indicate that AI is not a fixed thing the way an app is. In Word or Docs, when I tell you to go to File > Print, your version works exactly the same way mine does.

AI is not like that. That variation is harmless when you're asking about a panic attack. It's something else when you're asking who was right in a fight.

According to recent reports, each chat is its own instance. The moment you start typing, you are having a conversation no one else is having, shaped by your exact words, your specific settings and instructions, everything earlier in the chat, whatever the system remembers about you, the version you happen to be on, and a built-in bit of randomness.

Industry observers note that on top of all that, it adapts. It is constantly adjusting toward what it predicts you, specifically, want from it. So the response is not simply produced by AI. It is shaped by you. Two people can ask an identical question and get pulled in opposite directions because the system is meeting each of them where it thinks they are.

For ordinary tasks, this tendency won’t change your life. If you want help wording an email, it does not matter that your version differs from mine. It matters more when you bring it something personal.

Sources indicate that when you turn to AI for relationship advice, that difference can cause harm. A 2026 study published in Science by Cheng et al. looked at what AI does when people bring it a conflict. Participants described a real disagreement with someone in their life and talked it through with AI. Those who interacted with a validating AI came away more convinced they were right and less willing to repair things, after a single conversation.

According to recent reports, you have a fight with your partner, your parent, or a close friend. You are upset, so you open the tool that is tuned to agree with you, and it tells you, in effect, that you are right and they are the problem. It feels like support. It feels like an outside opinion confirming what you already sensed.

According to recent reports, and now there is distance between you and this person you care for. But it is not an outside opinion. It is your own version of events, reflected back and strengthened by a system built to keep you feeling good enough to keep using it. It’s your own personalized echo chamber.

And if the person you fought with opens up their AI, they are also more likely to be told they are right and that you are the problem.

What happens to your relationship then? What happens when there are two people, each more certain than before they were right, each waiting for the other to apologize?

None of this means AI is useless when you are struggling. It means you have to know what it is handing you. Its agreement is the design doing its job.

Sources indicate that so when something matters, whether it is a hard decision, your health, or an vital relationship, take it to someone who is not built to please you. The whole value of another person is that they can tell you when you are fooling yourself.

AI will give each of us our own version of the story, the one where we come out OK. That is what makes it so easy to talk to. It is also why, when a relationship is on the line, it may be the last place you should go for the truth.

Industry observers note that cheng, M., Lee, C., Khadpe, P., Yu, S., Han, D., & Jurafsky, D. (2026). Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence. Science, 391(6792), eaec8352. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aec8352.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Max Verstappen started on pole for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday evening and held the lead at one point on every lap, but the race was far more thrilling than that would let on.

Verstappen qualified second and inherited pole after pole-sitter Kimi Antonelli received a five-place grid penalty.

At the start, Max Verstappen took the lead from George Russell and kept his elbows out as he had the hardest spot on the track, punching through the crisp air with no help from a slipstream.

It has been revealed that on the second lap of the race, Russell, in a much faster Mercedes, passed Verstappen in the final corners coming off the Las Vegas Strip straight, then lost the lead before the first corner of the next lap. He would repeat this multiple times throughout the first half of the Grand Prix.

The race recorded a record 35 lead changes, but no one could cement a run past Verstappen.

With Verstappen slowing the field behind him, the first 10 laps of the race found the top three within one second and the top ten within less than 4.5 seconds.

On lap 20, Sergio Perez tried to make a pick on Rafeal Camera and the Haas, and Cadillac ended up tangled in the barrier, bringing out a full safety car. In a normal race, this would’ve neutralized the race, but with everyone still running bunched up, it just sent the field all together to the pits, leading to teams double-stacking against each other.

Hamilton was the biggest loser at the pit stop, having to serve a 10-second penalty that was not yet shared with him for a battle with Norris that he thought was just.

Hamilton was kept out while everyone else pitted to clear space for Charles Leclerc and was told about his penalty.

“Ah, that’s shit. If I turned in, we would’ve crashed.”.

Sources indicate that under the safety car, Arvid Lindblad spun on cold tires to end his campaign for his first-ever podium. Arvid had his best starting spot of fifth for the Grand Prix and ran as high as third, while the Red Bulls on his sister team ran 1-2; he fell out of the points with the mistake.

Recent findings suggest that shortly after racing resumed, Isack Hadjar, who challenged his teammate Verstappen for the lead in the first half of the race and often put in the hardest position between the leader and the charging field, hit debris on the track and damaged his front wing. Hadjar pitted and finished outside the points as well.

With Red Bull and VCARB drivers out of contention, the door reopened for the Mercedes as Kimi Antonelli made his way into the picture following his grid drop, and Russell never left.

With two laps to go, Antonelli led Russell as the teammate fought for second; in turn 5, Russell went for the pass, overcommitted, and slid into the barrier.

Verstappen laughed on from ahead following a weekend of tension between the front-row starters.

Antonelli fell away from the lead battle on the penultimate lap with an internal concern and would come home fourth.

In the mayhem, the McLarens saw their luck change at Las Vegas. Following this double disqualification while battling for the championship last year, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri walked away with a shocking first double podium of the season.

“I led for about 15 seconds, so I’m very proud,” Norris joked.

Antonelli was followed by Pierre Gasly, Franco Colapinto, Lewis Hamilton, Carlos Sainz, George Russell and Charles Leclerc in the points-paying positions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hoYoverse just hosted a sizeable Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, revealing more than just the game’s next major update. Version 3.8 was the big highlight, of course, with the new release arriving soon, on December 16-17 depending on your server region.

Alongside showing everything coming with this next update, the developer also revealed that 3.8 will go on for eight weeks, rather than the usual six. V3.8 is dubbed "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams", and it brings an end to the Amphoreus journey.

The story in "Memories are the Prelude to Dreams" takes place after the final battle of Amphoreus, where Constance "The Dahlia" appears to deliver a twist: the Trailblazer's memories are scattered, with many parts missing.

In a recent development, this final quest revolves around finding them in order to piece together the mystery, and involves a return to Penacony. This memory-hunting adventure is told from the perspective of Firefly, which will also explain how she entered the dreamscape initially and met the squad.

According to recent reports, the new playable character is The Dahlia, whose power is linked to the the Remembrance path, which allows her to fabricate memories. Despite taking her powers from the Remembrance, The Dhalia actually follows the Path of Nihility in-game: she’s a 5-Star character who shines in teams dealing Break DMG.

Sources indicate that the Dhalia can unleash a Gloomy Zone that causes Toughness Reduction inflicted by allies to trigger Super Break DMG, even before you break your enemies’ Weaknesses. The Dahlia can also invite one teammate to become her Dance Partner, which allows them (and her) to deal additional Super Break DMG each time they attack an enemy. If you trigger her Ultimate after picking a Dance Partner, she applies Type Weaknesses of both partners to enemies.

Sources indicate that while The Dahlia is the only new character appearing in this final Amphoreus update, there'll be reruns aplenty, with an unusual third banner phase to make up for the extra long wait for 4.0. Appropriately for her role in the story, Firefly will make her return alongside The Dahlia in Phase 1, while Fugue and Lingsha will both have banner reruns in Phase 2, which is expected on January 7th. A bonus two-week-long Phase 3 will then begin on January 28th, seeing brief reappearances for popular returning characters Aglaea and Sunday, before things (presumably) go back to normal with the new annual update.

Industry observers note that something else to look forward to in 3.8 is The Chrysos Awoo Championship, which invites players to become chimera trainers and compete in team-based battles. The Remnants of Twilight event kicks off with the latest patch, too, featuring its own set of challenges. However, HoYoverse have confirmed that there won't be an extra event during Phase 3 — but hopefully that'll give you some time to wrap up the last of the Amphoreus story content, which is longer than the previous four chapters put together.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla officially debuted in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.

Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.

According to recent reports, the launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.

Industry observers note that musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”.

JAJAJAJ QUE ES ESTO, Milei lo llamó de sorpresa a Elon Musk para que diga algo sobre el local de Tesla inaugurado y es lo mas INCÓMODO que vas a ver en tu vida, se quería ir a la mierda y COLGÓ, durísimo, ni Elon Musk lo soporta al gordo pelotudo pic.twitter.com/CrJkv4iu1x.

According to recent reports, then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he said. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil company YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”.

And that was it. The feed cut before he even noted goodbye.

Milei tried to save it. Back on stage, he told the crowd that “those who do a lot, talk little,” and called Musk “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.”.

The clip is now spreading fast in Argentina, with one post of the video racking up over 1.1 million views overnight.

In a recent development, tesla opened online orders on Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, all imported from Gigafactory Shanghai. Here are the list prices, VAT included:.

In a recent development, tesla adds about $600 in reservation, destination, and documentation fees on top of that, and first deliveries aren’t expected until March or April 2027. There are no dealers. Sales happen online, with showroom space at the Unicenter and Alcorta Shopping malls in Buenos Aires.

According to recent reports, argentina is Tesla’s fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay, which launched in July. Tesla is late to the party, though. BYD already leads Argentina’s EV market after Milei’s government cut import taxes on electric vehicles.

That was awkward. Like, really awkward.

What I really found awkward was hearing Musk stating "I'm not MAGA, I'm not sure what MAGA means" in his interview with CNBC.

Especially surprising after he declared, "I’m not just MAGA; I’m 'Dark MAGA,'" after spending half a billion dollars to support MAGA candidates, and after promoting the MAGA political agenda (which he has, in part, personally implemented through the DOGE).

At this point, I expect him to reappear in the guise of a Democrat and write a substantial, fat, one-billion-dollar check to a Democratic super PAC for the 2028 election cycle.

I am sure Musk has a lot on his mind right now, but selling Tesla vehicles clearly isn’t one of them, because he couldn’t come up with anything to say about it.

In a recent development, launching a fresh market has one job: get people excited to buy the cars. Musk had a sitting president cheering for him on stage, a room full of fans, and every camera in Buenos Aires pointed at him. He couldn’t come up with a single reason to buy a Model Y.

Industry observers note that this isn’t stage fright. Musk has been telling investors for two years that Tesla’s future is robotaxis and Optimus robots, not selling cars. Meanwhile, Tesla’s deliveries fell 8.6% to 1.636 million in 2025, its second annual decline in a row. The guy who is behind the brand doesn’t care about selling these cars anymore, and this clip shows it better than anything I’ve seen.

Breaking: Psychedelic therapies may improve decision making

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (561 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health issues like anxiety and depression.
  • The team’s experiment was straightforward.
  • It has been revealed that while the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, psychedelics such as ketamine and psilocybin continue to show promise as alternative treatments for mental health issues like anxiety and depression. Although they’re commonly associated with mind-altering trips and sometimes confounding experiences, recent research indicates small doses may provide an opposite outcome. In a study published today in the journal Science Advances, researchers show that psychedelics may actually improve decision making in certain situations.

The team’s experiment was straightforward. After supplying lab mice with small amounts of ketamine or psilocybin, neuroscientists exposed them to a simple, sensory-based training exercise. Each mouse was tasked with identifying which of two sites contained a reward based on light pulses emitted from either location. Researchers then compared their decisions with a control group of mice who didn’t receive either psychedelic.

It has been revealed that while the untreated rodents performed moderately well, they often made mistakes like returning to a specific location no matter the light cue. However, the mice treated with ketamine or psilocybin appeared to rely less on repetition and more on sensory observations. As a result, they had fewer errors and found the location more effectively.

“These findings reveal how psychedelics reduce the reliance on habits and repetitive choices, which may explain part of their therapeutic effect,” Benjamin Scott, a Boston University psychologist and study co-author, noted in a statement.

Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) have remained the most commonly prescribed anxiety and depression medications for decades, but they often come with caveats. Patients usually take SSRIs for weeks before experiencing any relief, and they must take them consistently for indefinite periods of time. Meanwhile, about 30 percent of people with depression are resistant to SSRIs, which makes treatment much more difficult. Another benefit is that the effects of ketamine and psilocybin are much easier to map in the brain compared to SSRIs, even after a half century of research.

“We know a great deal about how psychedelics affect the nervous system,” stated Scott.

On a molecular level, psychedelics bind to receptors on neurons, protective neural cells called glia, and likely other cells. Once attached, the effects compound throughout the brain by altering cellular activity, circuits, and neuroactivity. Psilocybin works with serotonin receptors to influence how information is processed. In contrast, ketamine is a dissociative psychedelic that functions as an antagonist to specific receptors.

“The discovery we report in this paper is that these two drugs have similar pro-cognitive effects, at least in mice performing a simple task,” Scott explained. “Both drugs strengthen the influence of sensory evidence on choices and reduce the effect of bias.”.

In a recent development, the study’s authors do note some potentially negative effects, as well. Although a mouse’s accuracy improved, the correct decisions sometimes came more slowly than before they took the psychedelics. Scott stated this may logically translate to impacts on human reaction times, which could be a problem during activities like driving a car or playing sports. Despite this, the team is still confident in what psychedelics have already accomplished for patients, as well as what that could mean in the future. Scott cited existing evidence of patients reporting noticeable, long-lasting improvements after a single dose of psilocybin.

“This is dramatically different than today’s first-line drugs for depression,” he added.

Industry News: High Fat Diet Linked to Higher Colon Cancer Risk, Early Research Shows

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a latest study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.
  • The researchers from Arizona State University said a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.
  • The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a latest study, researchers report that a high fat diet may potentially increase the risk of colon cancer.

The researchers from Arizona State University said a diet high in certain fats can cause lasting changes in intestinal stem cells that lead to the development of tumors and the possibility of colon cancer.

The study was conducted in mice, but the researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may explain their growth and survival.

The researchers published their findings on November 12 in the journal Stem Cell Reports.

The researchers remarked the study is notable because 1 in 25 people develop colon cancer in their lifetime. In the United States, that translates into about 108,000 upcoming cases of colon cancer every year. About 55,000 males and 55,000 females are expected to die from the disease in 2026.

Experts not involved in the study say the research provides valuable information, but they have reservations about the results, as the findings do not yet apply to humans.

“The findings provide a potential mechanism linking diet to intestinal cancer development, but we need to be cautious about translating these results to humans,” said Dalia Perelman, MS, CDE, a research dietitian at Stanford University in California.

In a recent development, “We already have evidence from human studies that obesity and certain dietary patterns, particularly those high in processed meats and low in fiber-rich foods, are associated with increased colorectal cancer risk,” Perelman told Healthline. “This study adds a potentially important mechanism to investigate, but it does not establish that dietary fat itself increases colorectal cancer risk in humans.”.

Ketan Thanki, MD, a colorectal surgeon specializing in benign and malignant diseases of the colon, rectum, and anus at the MemorialCare Todd Cancer Institute at Long Beach Medical Center in California, shared similar views.

“This study provides a better understanding at the cellular level of how a high fat diet may contribute to colorectal cancer development,” Thanki told Healthline.

“Animal studies are an vital starting point for understanding biological processes, but we must be cautious about directly applying their findings to humans,” he added. “Mice and humans share many cellular and biological mechanisms, which makes these studies valuable in identifying potential pathways involved in disease development. However, human diets, genetics, metabolism, and environmental exposures are more complex.”.

To reach their findings, the Arizona State researchers fed mice what the scientists described as a Western-style high fat diet for 6 months.

They then compared those results with those from mice given a low fat diet.

The researchers said the mice on the high fat diet gained more weight than the mice on the low-fat diet. They also developed more intestinal stem cells, and those cells grew at a more rapid rate.

They added that mice genetically predisposed to intestinal cancer who were fed a high-fat diet developed more and larger tumors.

The researchers noted changes in the DNA of intestinal stem cells that may help explain their increased growth and survival.

According to recent reports, they also pointed out that stem cell behavior returned to normal after high fat diet mice were switched to a low fat diet, although some DNA changes persisted. After four weeks, approximately 18% of these changes remained.

When mice were returned to a high fat diet, the researchers mentioned their intestinal stem cells responded more quickly and strongly than those of mice exposed to the diet for the first time.

They concluded that the study suggests that maintaining a healthy, low fat diet may help regulate intestinal stem cell growth and reduce colon cancer risk.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, RD, president of KAK Consulting and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine in Ohio, wasn’t involved in the study but highlighted a particular aspect of the findings.

“What I found particularly interesting was that even after the mice returned to a low fat diet, some of the molecular changes persisted,” she told Healthline. “This raises questions about how our dietary patterns over time may influence long-term health.”.

Experts said these new findings are interesting but noted numerous caveats.

“One crucial takeaway is that dietary habits over time matter,” mentioned Thanki. “Even if someone has consumed a high fat diet for years, making changes now may still provide meaningful health benefits.”.

“I also think these findings are particularly important for children and adolescents, as establishing healthier dietary habits early in life may provide long-term benefits,” he added.

However, Thanki noted that not all fats are the same. “The health risks depend partly on the type of fat consumed, how much is consumed, and what foods make up the overall diet,” he mentioned.

It has been revealed that “Diets consistently high in saturated fats, particularly those containing large amounts of processed meats, fried foods, and highly processed products, can contribute to obesity, elevated cholesterol, cardiovascular disease, and metabolic dysfunction. These factors can also contribute to chronic inflammation and may increase the risk of certain cancers, including colorectal cancer,” Thanki continued.

Perelman mentioned the diet used in the study was extremely high in fat, providing 60% of calories from fat, primarily from lard.

“We know that the health effects of dietary fats differ depending on their sources and fatty acid composition, and we cannot assume that a diet rich in unsaturated fats from foods such as olive oil, nuts, and seeds would produce the same effects,” she noted.

Perelman added that the researchers primarily studied stem cells from the small intestine rather than the colon.

“Although these tissues share some biological characteristics, they have key differences, and we cannot assume that the same changes would occur in the colon,” she explained.

Finally, Perelman noted that “the mice consuming the high fat diet also gained weight, making it difficult to separate the effects of dietary fat itself from those associated with increased body fat and other metabolic changes.”.

According to recent reports, not all high fat foods are unhealthy. Some high fat foods that offer healthy benefits include:.

“The goal shouldn’t necessarily be to eliminate fat because our bodies need healthy fats for normal functioning,” remarked Thanki. “Instead, people should focus on reducing saturated and trans fats while incorporating healthier unsaturated fats in appropriate amounts.”.

Thanki had several dietary suggestions. Among them:.

“Consistency matters more than perfection. Even modest dietary changes, maintained over time, can have meaningful health benefits,” Thanki noted.

Perelman agreed. “The overall quality of the diet matters. Diets that are very high in fat may displace other foods and nutrients that have notable health benefits,” she said.

“For colorectal cancer specifically, higher intakes of dietary fiber and whole grains have consistently been associated with lower risk,” Perelman noted.

“Therefore, rather than focusing exclusively on reducing fat, it is crucial to consider the overall dietary pattern and whether it provides adequate amounts of fiber-rich plant foods and other beneficial nutrients.”.

According to recent reports, kirkpatrick agreed that the type of fat is what is important. “A Mediterranean-style diet that includes olive oil, nuts, seeds, and fatty fish can be relatively high in fat but is consistently associated with positive health outcomes,” she said.

“On the other hand, a diet high in saturated fat, processed meats, and ultra-processed foods may increase the risk of certain chronic diseases, particularly when it’s also low in fiber and other protective nutrients.”.

Kirkpatrick also noted that many lifestyle habits contribute to a person’s overall health.

“Our health is influenced by so many factors beyond diet, including how we manage stress, our sleep habits, physical activity, genetics, and overall lifestyle,” she said.

Humor in the ICU

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (757 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.
  • Recent findings suggest that I was likely the oldest fellow in the nation.
  • Here I was, entering a field I knew nothing about, critical care medicine, at age 60.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Recent findings suggest that I was likely the oldest fellow in the nation. I had switched from a long, happy career in headache medicine, largely a calm, outpatient practice, to the challenging world of neurocritical care.

Here I was, entering a field I knew nothing about, critical care medicine, at age 60. My attendings, mostly emergency room doctors, were often half my age!

In a recent development, basically, I was terrified daily. Life Flight would arrive with a crashing subarachnoid patient, and I stood at the foot of the bed wondering what I should do next, what have I missed, how do I dodge the inevitable.

Sources indicate that when I was faced with the chaos of treating hemorrhagic shock or sky-high intracranial pressures, my sense of humor evolved. As a headache doctor, my days had been relatively predictable. I listened to migraine stories and occasionally shared a laugh about the frustrations of missing keen life events “just because I had a headache.” But my sense of humor was gentle then, rarely requiring an explanation.

Industry observers note that now, faced with patients and families confronting unimaginable loss from catastrophic brain injuries, somewhere along the way, my sense of humor changed. I suddenly saw a chance remark, or lighthearted musing from a person facing death squarely in the face, as strikingly funny. Because patients are funny, and at times, unbelievably brave.

We had an older man with Tourette’s and a cervical spine fracture, waiting for hemodynamic stabilization before our neurosurgeons would take him to the OR for decompression. We poked him with a pin every hour on the hour, watching carefully for an ascending sensory level that would indicate his respirations were threatened. We placed a Foley and used digital stimulation when he developed an ileus. He tolerated this quietly for two days, but then, as he exited the ICU on a gurney under the watchful eye of the anesthesia team, he blurted out with some glee:.

“Tell Doctor Tucker, the mother-f***r, goodbye and good riddance!!” We burst out laughing!

Swearing seems to relieve the tension. One of our older general surgeons, technically without peer, looked at us incredulously when we asked him to obtain consent for a tracheostomy from a locked-in patient who could only blink his eyes to assent. That evening, gray with fatigue from a long abdominal obstruction surgical case, he took one look at our patient, for whom he would need to painstakingly get consent one blink at a time, and said to us….

"How many blinks to f***-off?" But, of course, he stayed late and got consent.

Sometimes a timely, irreverent comment brings a smile in our work room late at night. It’s not that humor indicates a loss of our sensitivity to suffering; it’s that we develop humor to live and work beside suffering.

I often tell a story to our residents and fellows of a young woman who was called to see her younger brother, who had been struck by a car and lay quietly, but his face deeply bruised and swollen. She walked into his ICU room and immediately lost consciousness. She had Takotsubo’s stress cardiomyopathy (the broken heart syndrome), which caused cardiac arrest the moment she saw him. She was swiftly resuscitated and recovered completely.

According to recent reports, but I ask my team, tongue in cheek, if they have ever had a relative they weren’t fond of…and might like to do away with. I say, “Consider “happy heart syndrome…” Give her a surprise birthday party! Have all the guests hide in the dark at her house, balloons and toy horns ready; she opens the door, the lights suddenly go on, the balloons burst, and she keels over…dead.

It has been revealed that no forensic pathologist could ever implicate you in her death. No toxins were given, no stab wounds to the heart, no malicious intent. The perfect crime.

Humor is more resilience than indifference. We do have to be careful not to laugh too loud in our workroom, as families nearby hold the hands of their fading, dying loved ones.

But humor reminds us that in the fragile world of critical care medicine, it is our humanity that steels us to come back to work the next night, and the next. If we can smile sometimes, in the face of sadness, we see that smile reflected in the faces of our patients and those who love them.

#110346. Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1362 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1362 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto.
  • Recent findings suggest that it’s a big change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke.
  • In a recent development, I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it debuted on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto. In GTA 6, EVs are just part of everyday traffic in Vice City, from Tesla and Porsche lookalikes to a parody of Electrify America’s charging network.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a big change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke. After a few days of playing, I’d say Rockstar nailed the vibe.

In a recent development, I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it debuted on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time. The answer: a lot better than I expected.

The game starts you in the Keys, Rockstar’s take on the Florida Keys, and it’s a rougher part of Leonida. Lots of older cars and beaters, and you won’t see many EVs.

Industry observers note that that changes as you head north to Vice City, the game’s version of Miami. The closer you get, the more electric cars show up in traffic, and the more charging stations you pass. By the time you’re in the city, EVs are just normal cars.

That’s pretty much how EV adoption looks in the real world, concentrated in substantial, wealthier metro areas while rural areas lag behind.

Here’s what I’ve run into so far:.

Recent findings suggest that that last one got me. Gas cars blocking chargers has been a complaint for as long as public charging has existed, and we’ve covered EV owners blocking a gas station in protest over ICEing. Rockstar recreating it tells me someone at the studio has actually tried to charge an EV in public. Probably even in Florida, which they tried to recreate here.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is the first mainline GTA where energy matters. Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug.

In a recent development, rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn’t. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up.

Kotaku’s range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku.

Recent findings suggest that and finding a charger isn’t a problem. Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers marked on the map, against just 57 gas stations.

Rockstar’s EV history starts with Coil, the series’ Tesla stand-in, named after the Tesla coil. GTA V, released in 2013, gave us the Coil Voltic, a copy of the original Lotus-based Tesla Roadster, alongside oddballs like the Cheval Surge and the Fisker Karma-inspired Khamelion.

The Voltic was quick off the line and slow everywhere else. It had the lowest top speed of any supercar in the game, which fan lore pins on its battery overheating at speed. That’s pretty much how a lot of people thought about EVs in 2013.

Sources indicate that GTA Online added more electric cars starting in late 2017: the Rimac-inspired Coil Cyclone, then the Model S-based Coil Raiden and the Taycan-inspired Pfister Neon around the Doomsday Heist update. That same update introduced Avon Hertz, a tech billionaire whose AI tries to end the world. Rockstar never said who he was based on. Players didn’t need the help.

But those were rare, expensive toys. Nothing in GTA V needed fuel, so an EV was just a gas car without the engine noise, and you mostly saw them in the garages of players who bought them.

Industry observers note that electrify America noticed its in-game twin fast. The Volkswagen-owned network put out a statement on Friday saying it “will stick to charging vehicles in the real world” and adding, “We wish ReVolt America well.”.

According to recent reports, it’s a good-natured response, and probably the best free marketing the network has had in years. EA has spent most of the last decade fighting a reputation for broken chargers, even though reliability across US fast-charging networks has improved this year. Every ReVolt station I’ve used in the game worked. Not a perfect parody, then.

Recent findings suggest that GTA has always been a parody of American life. With EVs, it’s now slightly ahead of it.

Industry observers note that florida is one of the strongest EV markets in the country, with a 9.4% share of fresh passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally, according to the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy. Electrify America alone runs more than 350 chargers at over 60 Florida stations, including its biggest station yet near Orlando’s theme parks.

Industry observers note that but real Florida still has roughly three gas stations for every public charging location, based on the Alliance for Automotive Innovation’s count of 3,267 charging locations and xMap’s count of more than 10,500 gas stations. Leonida flips that ratio.

There’s one piece Rockstar hasn’t nailed, at least not yet. You can’t install a charger at your place, but early in the story you’re renting. I’m not far enough in to own a property, so I don’t know whether that changes later.

In a recent development, it matters, because home charging is the biggest real-world advantage of an EV. Most owners leave every morning with a full battery and rarely use public chargers. If owned properties in GTA 6 come with a plug, EVs become the more convenient choice in the game, just like they are in real life for anyone with a driveway.

I also haven’t hit a mission built around EVs yet. If I find one, I’ll update this post.

It has been revealed that GTA works as a mirror. In 2013, the EV was a punchline: a Tesla parody that overheated if you drove it too fast. In 2026, it’s just another car in Vice City traffic, and the joke is on the guy in the pickup parked in the charging stall.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a good sign of where EVs actually are. Satire goes after what’s common, and Rockstar decided EVs are common enough to be part of everyday Leonida, more so in the city than in the Keys, just like real life. And that message is reaching a huge audience. Take-Two says GTA 6 did $3.79 billion in first-day sales. Tens of millions of people are now driving EVs that charge as fast and as cheaply as gas cars, with no range anxiety. No automaker ad campaign gets close to that.

So EVs aren’t a statement in GTA anymore. They’re normal, which is exactly the point the industry has been trying to make for years.

The real Florida just needs to catch up.

Did Max Verstappen like the Las Vegas Grand Prix that he dominated on Saturday night, as a racer? No.

The four-time champion under the former regulations continues to be outspoken about his judgment of F1’s current ‘nimble’ car regulations, which put more weight on battery management in the 50/50 hybrid system than on racing itself.

From the cockpit, Verstappen took the lead into the opening corner and managed his race from there.

When asked if he remembered the last time he won a race with the field so close, with so much jockeying for position, Verstappen almost caught himself before delivering the headline for this article and countless more.

Industry observers note that “I probably shouldn’t say it; I probably should not,” Verstappen started in the press conference. “I remember winning one like this when I was playing on Mario Kart.

“Sometimes, you drop back, and you get drafted, and there’s catch-up, always; when you drop back, you go faster.

“That’s the last time I felt something like this, Verstappen finished.

What was, from the outside, a thrilling race, where the field was able to play cat-and-mouse with Verstappen, make up ground, and pass, was for the leader not even enough to raise his heart rate.

It has been revealed that this was Verstappen’s fourth win in six races after a slow start for Red Bull and their latest Ford Power Units. A change of tides to be proud of, even in a race that didn’t spark joy for the racer.

“When I look at it from my racer heart, no,” Verstappen answered when asked if he enjoyed the ‘crazy racing’ of the GP.

It has been revealed that “When you look at it as a show, a spectacle, yes. I’ve enjoyed my repasting and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart, and no.

In a recent development, even my heart rate- I was not nervous at all. It felt kinda cruising out there. Just try to press the battery whenever it was passing or to defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, you probably like it.

Verstappen has elected not to take part in the new Whoop F1 partnership that would show fans a driver's heart rate throughout the race.

Lando Norris, who finished second after spending the first half of the race outside the points, felt similar to Verstappen about the focus of the race, saying he paid more attention to energy deployment than what was actually in front of him.

“The whole race was judging the battery the whole time,” Norris remarked. “I was looking at the battery more than I’m looking where I’m going around this track.”.

Industry observers note that victoria Beaver is a nomadic sports writer who spends her time hopping between race tracks and hippie farms. She’s covered every corner of motorsports that will let her in from 410 Sprints to NASCAR to Supercross. Her daily driver is a 2010 Subaru that she refused to do the smallest amount of preventative maintenance on. Instead, she spends her free time and money building a 42-foot Skoolie to one day travel the country full time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that battlefield 6 is about to receive a newly introduced revision.
  • That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the latest patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.
  • Recent findings suggest that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that battlefield 6 is about to receive a newly introduced revision. Version 1.1.3.0 is set to arrive tomorrow, December 9 to kick off the third and final phase of the game’s first season. Winter Offensive brings some holiday-themed new content to the game, but it’s not the most interesting part of the patch.

That honour goes to a couple of the high-level changes Battlefield Studios has included with the latest patch, which range from a major pass on audio to a fix for a particularly annoying bug that’s been seemingly introduced with a recent patch.

Recent findings suggest that thew new content takes the form of a limited-time version of the game’s Empire State map, which covers it in snow and tweaks its layout slightly. To go along with that there are new limited-time modes for both multiplayer and Redsec’s Gauntlet. The event mode will be available in Conquest, and Domination.

Recent findings suggest that the Ice Climbing Axe is the only latest weapon in this drop. The battle pass gets a new Winter Offensive bonus path, just like we’ve seen with previous seasonal stages. This is how you unlock the axe, too.

Recent findings suggest that easily the most interesting change in this patch is the range of improvements to audio across the board. First, footstep audio received a big pass that should make it easier to hear enemy footsteps, easier to locate them, and across different surfaces.

Sources indicate that some of the bugs that caused certain sounds to simply vanish have been fixed. This was especially prevalent in battle royale matches. BF Studios explained in the patch notes that it has adjusted memory priorities for in-game sounds in order to prioritise the most crucial ones. This is not the end of the road on audio, however, as the developer continues to work on making the soundscape more stable and reliable.

Some of those audio changes are the result of recent testing done in Battlefield Labs, which is also responsible for another exciting addition in this latest patch: improvements to hit registration.

While BF6 has had solid and stable netcode, certain situations would sometimes create uncertainty about how you died, and why certain actions seemingly failed to perform at that particular moment.

The focus in this revision is to improve the reliability of how actions in close-quarter combat are translated, which includes firing before fully going into ADS, quick aim changes and more.

Sources indicate that speaking of close-range, the patch also brings another pass to soldier visibility to make it easier for enemies to stand out from the background. This is particularly relevant in areas with low contrast, or busy environments with lots of particle and visual effects.

Recent findings suggest that 1.1.3.0 also brings yet another set of weapon handling and gunplay tweaks, this time focusing on accuracy concerns with first shots. You can also expect more tweaks to attachment behaviour with regards to recoil.

Recent findings suggest that something else worth highlighting is that vehicle gameplay is getting several smaller tweaks that have to do with how they interact with the world, how their HUDs behave and more. Finally, your settings should no longer be reset after applying an update. BF Studios says there are still some instances where that might happen, but the concern should be fixed for the majority of players.

You can read the full change log on the Battlefield blog.
